title: TechGraphRAG: An Agentic Graph-Augmented RAG Framework for Technical Literature Reasoning
authors: Kanwar Bharat Singh
why_relevant: Implements evidence sufficiency scoring and agentic retry/external search when local evidence is weak, touching on control/calibration aspects of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific case study without rigorous robustness evaluation; focuses on engineering pipeline rather than robustness, conflicts, or adversarial issues.

title: Text-Graph Synergy: A Bidirectional Verification and Completion Framework for RAG
authors: Jiarui Zhong; Hong Cai Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a hybrid text-graph RAG framework that re-ranks textual evidence to filter pseudo-evidence/semantic noise, touching on noisy retrieval issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is multi-hop reasoning performance via text-graph synergy, not robustness, calibration, conflict, or adversarial settings.

title: The Autonomy Tax: Defense Training Breaks LLM Agents
authors: Shawn Li; Yue Zhao
why_relevant: Studies how defense training against prompt injection breaks LLM agents, tangentially related to robustness against malicious retrieved/observed content.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent tool-use rather than RAG specifically; emphasis is on capability degradation from defenses, not retrieval robustness or calibration.

title: The Geometry of Forgetting: Temporal Knowledge Drift as an Independent Axis in LLM Representations
authors: Rania Elbadry; Ahmed Heakl; Fan Zhang; Dani Bouch; Yuxia Wang; Preslav Nakov; Zhuohan Xie
why_relevant: Studies internal detection of temporally stale parametric knowledge, which relates to knowing when to retrieve (selective retrieval trigger) and uncertainty about parametric vs external knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Not about RAG robustness per se; focuses on representational geometry of temporal drift in LLMs, with only brief mention of selective retrieval.

title: Theoretical Foundations and Mitigation of Hallucination in Large Language Models
authors: Esmail Gumaan
why_relevant: Theoretical treatment of hallucination with discussion of detection, calibration, and RAG as mitigation, tangentially related to robust RAG themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Not focused on RAG robustness, unreliable evidence, conflict, or attacks; treats RAG only briefly as one mitigation among many.

title: To Memorize or to Retrieve: Scaling Laws for RAG-Considerate Pretraining
authors: Karan Singh; Michael Yu; Varun Gangal; Zhuofu Tao; Sachin Kumar; Emmy Liu; Steven Y. Feng
why_relevant: Studies scaling laws trading off parametric vs retrieval knowledge allocation; tangentially relevant to when to rely on retrieval vs internal knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Does not address robustness, noise, conflict, adversarial attacks, calibration, or abstention; focused on pretraining/retrieval data allocation.

title: Token-Guard: Towards Token-Level Hallucination Control via Self-Checking Decoding
authors: Yifan Zhu; Huiqiang Rong; Haoran Luo
why_relevant: Proposes a decoding-time hallucination control method evaluated on HALU benchmarks; tangentially related to reliability of LLM generation but not focused on RAG robustness under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Not about retrieval noise, conflict, adversarial documents, or RAG calibration; orthogonal decoding approach.

title: Topic Is Not Agenda: A Citation-Community Audit of Text Embeddings
authors: Junseon Yoo
why_relevant: Audits embedding-based retrieval failures at fine granularity, exposing a concrete failure mode of scientific RAG where top neighbors are off-agenda, which relates to noisy/imprecise retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on embedding semantics vs citation communities rather than robustness, conflict, adversarial, or calibration aspects central to the survey.

title: Towards Better Generalization in Open-Domain Question Answering by Mitigating Context Memorization
authors: Zixuan Zhang; Revanth Gangi Reddy; Kevin Small; Tong Zhang; Heng Ji
why_relevant: Addresses reader over-memorization of retrieved corpus, which relates to parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge reliance and generalization to updated/new corpora (distribution shift).
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on generalization across corpus updates/domains rather than directly on robustness to noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence.

title: Towards Copyright Protection for Knowledge Bases of Retrieval-augmented Language Models via Reasoning
authors: Junfeng Guo; Yiming Li; Ruibo Chen; Yihan Wu; Chenxi Liu; Yanshuo Chen; Heng Huang
why_relevant: Proposes watermarking for copyright protection of RAG knowledge bases via CoT, tangentially related to RAG security but focused on IP protection rather than robustness against unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Not about robustness, conflict, calibration, or defending against adversarial retrieval; uses backdoor-like techniques for ownership verification.

title: Towards Lighter and Robust Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Alex-Razvan Ispas; Charles-Elie Simon; Fabien Caspani; Vincent Guigue
why_relevant: Proposes a lightweight open-weight LLM-as-judge metric for RAG correctness and faithfulness, tangentially relevant to evaluation of hallucination in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on cost-efficient evaluation methodology rather than robustness to noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence or calibration.

title: Towards Reliable Medical LLMs: Benchmarking and Enhancing Confidence Estimation of Large Language Models in Medical Consultation
authors: Zhiyao Ren; Yibing Zhan; Siyuan Liang; Guozheng Ma; Baosheng Yu; Dacheng Tao
why_relevant: Proposes a confidence estimation benchmark and method (MedConf) that uses RAG to ground confidence in supporting/missing/contradictory evidence relations, touching on calibration and evidence sufficiency.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is medical confidence estimation in multi-turn consultations, not robust RAG per se; RAG is a component, not the object of study.

title: Towards Transparent RAG: Fostering Evidence Traceability in LLM Generation via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jingyi Ren; Yekun Xu; Xiaolong Wang; Weitao Li; Ante Wang; Weizhi Ma; Yang Liu
why_relevant: Proposes RL-based evidence attribution/citation for RAG, which touches on transparency and grounding under retrieved context but does not directly study noise, conflict, adversaries, or calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on traceability/citation in multi-hop QA, not on robustness to unreliable evidence per se.

title: Traceable Cross-Source RAG for Chinese Tibetan Medicine Question Answering
authors: Fengxian Chen; Zhilong Tao; Jiaxuan Li; Yunlong Li; Qingguo Zhou
why_relevant: Domain-specific RAG system for Tibetan medicine addressing source bias and cross-source evidence fusion with traceability/citation metrics, tangentially related to noisy retrieval and evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily an applied domain system; does not centrally study robustness, conflict, adversarial, or calibration issues in a generalizable way.

title: Trust but Verify: Introducing DAVinCI -- A Framework for Dual Attribution and Verification in Claim Inference for Language Models
authors: Vipula Rawte; Ryan Rossi; Franck Dernoncourt; Nedim Lipka
why_relevant: Proposes an attribution+verification pipeline with confidence recalibration for claim verification, touching on calibration and evidence-based verification relevant to RAG reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on fact-checking on FEVER rather than robust RAG under noisy/adversarial evidence; not central to survey scope.

title: TrustRAG: An Information Assistant with Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Yixing Fan; Qiang Yan; Wenshan Wang; Jiafeng Guo; Ruqing Zhang; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: TrustRAG is a system/framework with utility-based filtering and citation enhancement aimed at trustworthiness, tangentially relating to filtering noisy retrieval and attribution.
why_not_or_caveat: Demo paper focused on engineering a framework; does not systematically study robustness, conflict, adversaries, or calibration.

title: Trustful LLMs: Customizing and Grounding Text Generation with Knowledge Bases and Dual Decoders
authors: Xiaofeng Zhu; Jaya Krishna Mandivarapu
why_relevant: Proposes post-processing with knowledge triplets and a dual-decoder to ground LLM outputs in RAG context, addressing hallucinations against retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on grounding/hallucination correction in a commercial application; does not systematically study noise, adversarial corruption, calibration, or robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Understanding Inequality of LLM Fact-Checking over Geographic Regions with Agent and Retrieval models
authors: Bruno Coelho; Shujaat Mirza; Yuyuan Cui; Christina Pöpper; Damon McCoy
why_relevant: Evaluates LLM fact-checking accuracy across regions with RAG and agent-based retrieval, touching on retrieval limitations for region-specific knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on geographic bias in fact-checking, not on robustness of RAG to unreliable evidence, conflict, or adversarial inputs.

title: Unlearning Climate Misinformation in Large Language Models
authors: Michael Fore; Simranjit Singh; Chaehong Lee; Amritanshu Pandey; Antonios Anastasopoulos; Dimitrios Stamoulis
why_relevant: Examines poisoning LLMs with climate misinformation and compares unlearning, finetuning, and RAG as mitigation. Touches on misinformation defense but focuses on model unlearning rather than RAG robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: RAG is only one of several mitigations evaluated; not centrally about retrieval robustness, conflict, or calibration.

title: VectorSmuggle: Steganographic Exfiltration in Embedding Stores and a Cryptographic Provenance Defense
authors: Jascha Wanger
why_relevant: Studies steganographic exfiltration via embedding perturbations in RAG vector stores and proposes a cryptographic provenance defense. Tangentially related to adversarial corruption of RAG pipelines but focused on data exfiltration/integrity rather than retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Threat model is insider exfiltration, not poisoning/injection that misleads RAG outputs; orthogonal to robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: VeriCite: Towards Reliable Citations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Rigorous Verification
authors: Haosheng Qian; Yixing Fan; Jiafeng Guo; Ruqing Zhang; Qi Chen; Dawei Yin; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: VeriCite addresses citation/attribution reliability in RAG via NLI-based evidence verification, tangentially related to filtering noisy evidence and hallucination mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on citation generation quality rather than robustness against noise, conflict, adversarial inputs, or calibration/abstention.

title: VeriFact: Verifying Facts in LLM-Generated Clinical Text with Electronic Health Records
authors: Philip Chung; Akshay Swaminathan; Alex J. Goodell; Yeasul Kim; S. Momsen Reincke; Lichy Han; Ben Deverett; Mohammad Amin Sadeghi; Abdel-Badih Ariss; Marc Ghanem; David Seong; Andrew A. Lee; Caitlin E. Coombes; Brad Bradshaw; Mahir A. Sufian; Hyo Jung Hong; Teresa P. Nguyen; Mohammad R. Rasouli; Komal Kamra; Mark A. Burbridge; James C. McAvoy; Roya Saffary; Stephen P. Ma; Dev Dash; James Xie; Ellen Y. Wang; Clifford A. Schmiesing; Nigam Shah; Nima Aghaeepour
why_relevant: Uses RAG + LLM-as-judge to fact-check clinical text against EHRs; tangentially relates to factual verification but not focused on RAG robustness, noise, conflict, or adversarial issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Application-oriented system for clinical fact-checking; does not study retrieval robustness, distraction, conflicts, attacks, or calibration.

title: When "Better" Prompts Hurt: Evaluation-Driven Iteration for LLM Applications
authors: Daniel Commey
why_relevant: Proposes an evaluation suite that includes RAG compliance and groundedness, touching on calibration and evaluation practices. However, it is a general LLM evaluation workflow paper, not focused on robustness under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Scope is broad prompt-iteration evaluation; RAG robustness is a minor component with small toy experiments.

title: When Small Models Are Right for Wrong Reasons: Process Verification for Trustworthy Agents
authors: Laksh Advani
why_relevant: Studies reasoning integrity in small models and finds RAG improves grounding while self-critique harms it; tangentially touches process verification relevant to trustworthy RAG agents.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on process-level reasoning verification, not on robustness of RAG to unreliable evidence; uses oracle context rather than studying noisy/conflicting/adversarial retrieval.

title: Why Neighborhoods Matter: Traversal Context and Provenance in Agentic GraphRAG
authors: Riccardo Terrenzi; Maximilian von Zastrow; Serkan Ayvaz
why_relevant: Studies citation faithfulness and provenance in Agentic GraphRAG via ablations, touching on evaluation of grounding reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on citation/provenance in graph traversal rather than robustness to noise, conflict, adversaries, or calibration; small-scale and tangential.

title: Zero2Text: Zero-Training Cross-Domain Inversion Attacks on Textual Embeddings
authors: Doohyun Kim; Donghwa Kang; Kyungjae Lee; Hyeongboo Baek; Brent Byunghoon Kang
why_relevant: Proposes an embedding inversion attack against vector databases used in RAG, touching on privacy risks of RAG infrastructure.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/inversion attacks rather than robustness of RAG generation under unreliable evidence; out of scope for noise/conflict/calibration themes.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23229)] Fine-Grained Privacy Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Knowledge Asymmetry Exploitation
why_relevant: Proposes a privacy extraction attack on RAG systems, tangentially related to adversarial threats against RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy leakage rather than robustness to unreliable evidence, conflict, calibration, or distraction.

title: \[[RAGSynth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10989)\] RAGSynth: Synthetic Data for Robust and Faithful RAG Component Optimization
why_relevant: Proposes synthetic data generation to improve retriever robustness for domain-specific RAG and introduces a benchmark with varying answerability and hop counts, tangentially related to retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retriever optimization via synthetic data for domain adaptation rather than addressing noise, conflict, adversarial attacks, calibration, or distraction in RAG.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14888)\] Privacy Implications of Retrieval-Based Language Models
why_relevant: Studies privacy leakage from kNN-LM datastores, an orthogonal reliability concern to robustness under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/data extraction, not noise, conflict, adversarial poisoning of retrieval, calibration, or evidence reliability.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07914)\] Can Knowledge Graphs Reduce Hallucinations in LLMs? : A Survey
why_relevant: Survey on KG-augmented LLMs to reduce hallucinations, tangentially related to grounding LLMs with external knowledge but not focused on robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on KG augmentation for hallucination reduction, not on noise, conflict, adversarial attacks, or calibration in RAG.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16893)\] The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
why_relevant: Studies privacy extraction attacks on RAG retrieval databases, tangentially related to adversarial robustness of RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on privacy leakage, not on robustness to unreliable evidence, conflict, or calibration.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14773)\] Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data
why_relevant: Addresses privacy leakage in RAG via synthetic retrieval data, tangentially related to robustness against data exposure but not core robustness topics (noise, conflict, adversarial attacks on outputs, calibration).
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy preservation rather than reliability under unreliable evidence.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07589)\] No Free Lunch: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Undermines Fairness in LLMs, Even for Vigilant Users
why_relevant: Studies how RAG can undermine fairness alignment in LLMs via biased external datasets, tangentially related to unreliable evidence and corruption risks.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on fairness/bias rather than robustness, noise, conflict, or calibration central to the survey scope.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20142)\] Mask-based Membership Inference Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a membership inference attack against RAG knowledge databases, which relates to privacy/security threats on RAG systems but not to robustness under unreliable evidence per se.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on privacy attacks (MIA), not on noise/distraction/conflict/calibration or defenses against poisoning.
suggested_section: Adversarial and privacy threats to RAG

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09136)\] Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG
why_relevant: Survey on Agentic RAG covering adaptive retrieval workflows, which tangentially relates to calibration/control aspects like when to retrieve and re-retrieve.
why_not_or_caveat: Does not focus on robustness, noise, conflict, adversarial attacks, or calibration; only general overview of agentic RAG architectures.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17390)\] Mitigating Bias in RAG: Controlling the Embedder
why_relevant: Studies bias conflict among RAG components (embedder, LLM, corpus), which tangentially relates to knowledge conflict in RAG but focuses on social bias rather than reliability/robustness under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on fairness/bias mitigation, not on noise, adversarial corruption, calibration, or factual reliability central to the survey.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18910)\] A Systematic Review of Key Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems: Progress, Gaps, and Future Directions
why_relevant: General systematic review of RAG progress, covering architectures, applications, and some challenges but not focused on robustness, conflict, adversarial attacks, or calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Broad overview survey without dedicated focus on unreliable evidence; only tangentially touches challenges like retrieval quality and privacy.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.13000)] RAGE Against the Machine: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Explanations
why_relevant: Tool for counterfactual explanations of RAG outputs, identifying which retrieved sources affect answers; tangentially related to provenance and position bias but not robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on explainability/provenance, not on noise, conflict, attacks, or calibration.

title: mRAG: Elucidating the Design Space of Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Chan-Wei Hu; Yueqi Wang; Shuo Xing; Chia-Ju Chen; Suofei Feng; Ryan Rossi; Zhengzhong Tu
why_relevant: Studies multimodal RAG design space including re-ranking and self-reflection to suppress irrelevant context, tangentially touching noisy retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is pipeline design and performance optimization, not robustness, conflict, attacks, or calibration.

title: vLLM Hook v0: A Plug-in for Programming Model Internals on vLLM
authors: Ching-Yun Ko; Pin-Yu Chen
why_relevant: A vLLM plug-in tool whose demo use cases include prompt injection detection and RAG re-ranking via attention heads, tangentially touching robust RAG concerns.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily an engineering tool paper, not a study of RAG robustness, conflict, calibration, or adversarial defenses per se.

title: "Glue pizza and eat rocks" -- Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models
authors: Zhen Tan; Chengshuai Zhao; Raha Moraffah; Yifan Li; Song Wang; Jundong Li; Tianlong Chen; Huan Liu
why_relevant: Proposes LIAR, a bi-level attack that injects adversarial documents into RAG knowledge bases to be preferentially retrieved and manipulate LLM outputs in a gray-box setting, directly addressing RAG poisoning vulnerabilities.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and poisoning attacks on RAG

title: ADMIT: Few-shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based Fact Checking
authors: Yutao Wu; Xiao Liu; Yinghui Li; Yifeng Gao; Yifan Ding; Jiale Ding; Xiang Zheng; Xingjun Ma
why_relevant: Proposes a few-shot knowledge poisoning attack against RAG-based fact-checking that remains effective even when credible counter-evidence dominates the retrieval pool, directly addressing adversarial corruption and conflict robustness in RAG.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Jian Xie; Kai Zhang; Jiangjie Chen; Renze Lou; Yu Su
why_relevant: Seminal controlled study of LLM behavior under knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and retrieved evidence, revealing receptivity to coherent counter-evidence and confirmation bias with mixed evidence.

title: AdversarialCoT: Single-Document Retrieval Poisoning for LLM Reasoning
authors: Hongru Song; Yu-An Liu; Ruqing Zhang; Jiafeng Guo; Maarten de Rijke; Yixing Fan; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes a single-document corpus poisoning attack against RAG that targets reasoning LLMs via adversarial CoT, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qingying Niu; Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Bohui Fang; Wayne Xin Zhao
why_relevant: ArbGraph directly addresses conflict resolution and noise suppression in RAG by arbitrating evidence credibility through a conflict-aware graph before generation, targeting retrieved-vs-retrieved conflicts and noisy long-form RAG.

title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
authors: Fei Wang; Xingchen Wan; Ruoxi Sun; Jiefeng Chen; Sercan Ö. Arık
why_relevant: Astute RAG directly addresses imperfect retrieval and knowledge conflicts by adaptively eliciting internal knowledge and consolidating it with retrieved evidence in a source-aware manner, with analyses of retrieval quality vs conflict rate.

title: BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Jiaqi Xue; Mengxin Zheng; Yebowen Hu; Fei Liu; Xun Chen; Qian Lou
why_relevant: BadRAG introduces a corpus-poisoning backdoor attack on RAG retrievers that triggers denial-of-service and sentiment steering in downstream LLMs, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiawei Chen; Hongyu Lin; Xianpei Han; Le Sun
why_relevant: RGB benchmark evaluates LLM RAG on noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness—directly aligned with the survey's themes of noisy evidence, conflict, and abstention.

title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang; Haoran Xin; Jiatong Li; Dongzhe Zhang; Minghong Fang; Zhuqing Liu; Lihai Nie; Zheli Liu
why_relevant: Provides a comprehensive benchmark of 13 poisoning attacks and 7 defenses against RAG across multiple architectures, directly addressing adversarial corruption and evaluation under unreliable evidence.

title: Beyond Black-Box Interventions: Latent Probing for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Linfeng Gao; Qinggang Zhang; Baolong Bi; Bo Zeng; Zheng Yuan; Zerui Chen; Zhimin Wei; Shenghua Liu; Linlong Xu; Longyue Wang; Weihua Luo; Jinsong Su
why_relevant: Proposes ProbeRAG, using latent-space probing to detect knowledge conflicts and filter noisy context, directly addressing faithfulness under unreliable evidence.

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
authors: Björn Deiseroth; Max Henning Höth; Kristian Kersting; Letitia Parcalabescu
why_relevant: Proposes a training framework with adversarial (Morgana) and helpful (Merlin) provers to make RAG generators abstain on insufficient evidence, resist misleading context, and ground in causal evidence, with information-theoretic guarantees. Directly targets hallucination, reject behavior, and robustness to adversarial/noisy context.

title: CUB: Benchmarking Context Utilisation Techniques for Language Models
authors: Lovisa Hagström; Youna Kim; Haeun Yu; Sang-goo Lee; Richard Johansson; Hyunsoo Cho; Isabelle Augenstein
why_relevant: CUB is a purpose-built benchmark for evaluating context utilisation manipulation techniques in RAG under gold, conflicting, and irrelevant contexts, directly covering noisy retrieval, distraction, and knowledge conflict.

title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
authors: Chong Xiang; Tong Wu; Zexuan Zhong; David Wagner; Danqi Chen; Prateek Mittal
why_relevant: Proposes RobustRAG, the first certifiably robust defense framework against retrieval corruption (PoisonedRAG, indirect prompt injection) using isolate-then-aggregate strategy.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Wenhao Yu; Hongming Zhang; Xiaoman Pan; Kaixin Ma; Hongwei Wang; Dong Yu
why_relevant: Chain-of-Note directly targets RAG robustness to noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents and unknown-question abstention, key topics of the survey.

title: CleanBase: Detecting Malicious Documents in RAG Knowledge Databases
authors: Weifei Jin; Xilong Wang; Wei Zou; Jinyuan Jia; Neil Gong
why_relevant: Proposes a defense to detect malicious documents in RAG knowledge bases against prompt injection/poisoning attacks, directly addressing adversarial corruption of evidence.

title: CoRect: Context-Aware Logit Contrast for Hidden State Rectification to Resolve Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Xuhua Ma; Richong Zhang; Zhijie Nie
why_relevant: Proposes a training-free hidden-state intervention to resolve parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflicts in RAG, directly addressing context compliance.

title: Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Eunseong Choi; June Park; Hyeri Lee; Jongwuk Lee
why_relevant: Proposes CARE, a conflict-aware soft prompting method that helps RAG resolve context-memory conflicts via grounded/adversarial training, directly addressing knowledge conflict and reliability of retrieved evidence.

title: Confundo: Learning to Generate Robust Poison for Practical RAG Systems
authors: Haoyang Hu; Zhejun Jiang; Yueming Lyu; Junyuan Zhang; Yi Liu; Ka-Ho Chow
why_relevant: Proposes a learning-to-poison framework targeting practical RAG pipelines, addressing chunking-induced fragmentation and lexical generalization, and evaluates against defenses across multiple attack objectives.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning Attacks on RAG

title: Context-DPO: Aligning Language Models for Context-Faithfulness
authors: Baolong Bi; Shaohan Huang; Yiwei Wang; Tianchi Yang; Zihan Zhang; Haizhen Huang; Lingrui Mei; Junfeng Fang; Zehao Li; Furu Wei; Weiwei Deng; Feng Sun; Qi Zhang; Shenghua Liu
why_relevant: Proposes Context-DPO alignment to improve context-faithfulness under knowledge conflicts in RAG, and introduces ConFiQA benchmark with counterfactual contexts for evaluation.

title: Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework
authors: Lu Chen; Ruqing Zhang; Jiafeng Guo; Yixing Fan; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes a counterfactual prompting framework for risk control in RAG, enabling abstention based on retrieval quality and usage, with new risk-related metrics and benchmark.
suggested_section: Calibration and control: abstention in RAG

title: CtrlRAG: Black-box Document Poisoning Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Runqi Sui
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box document poisoning attack against RAG and a defense based on parametric/non-parametric memory confrontation, directly addressing adversarial corruption and conflict-based defense.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning Attacks and Defenses

title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs
authors: Arie Cattan; Alon Jacovi; Ori Ram; Jonathan Herzig; Roee Aharoni; Sasha Goldshtein; Eran Ofek; Idan Szpektor; Avi Caciularu
why_relevant: Proposes a taxonomy of RAG knowledge conflicts (freshness, opinion, misinformation, complementary) and introduces CONFLICTS, an expert-annotated benchmark for evaluating how LLMs resolve conflicting retrieved sources, directly addressing the survey's conflict and evaluation dimensions.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
authors: Yanbo Dai; Zhenlan Ji; Zongjie Li; Kuan Li; Shuai Wang
why_relevant: Introduces a novel retriever-poisoning attack that suppresses LLM self-correction ability, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and context-vs-parametric conflict robustness in RAG.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
authors: Xin Sun; Jianan Xie; Zhongqi Chen; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Yuehe Chen; Bowen Song; Weiqiang Wang; Zilei Wang; Liang Wang
why_relevant: Proposes DPO-based alignment for RAG to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries, directly addressing calibration, abstention, and noisy retrieval robustness.

title: Do Retrieval Augmented Language Models Know When They Don't Know?
authors: Youchao Zhou; Heyan Huang; Yicheng Liu; Rui Dai; Xinglin Wang; Xingchen Zhang; Shumin Shi; Yang Deng
why_relevant: Studies calibration, refusal/abstention, and over-refusal in RALMs under irrelevant retrieved contexts, directly addressing uncertainty estimation and control under unreliable evidence.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Sunguk Shin; Meeyoung Cha; Byung-Jun Lee; Sungwon Park
why_relevant: ERA directly addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence, uses evidential deep learning and Dempster-Shafer theory to calibrate confidence, and enables abstention under unsupported queries — central themes of the survey.
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention under Knowledge Conflict

title: EcoSafeRAG: Efficient Security through Context Analysis in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ruobing Yao; Yifei Zhang; Shuang Song; Neng Gao; Chenyang Tu
why_relevant: Proposes a defense framework against RAG poisoning, prompt injection, and adversarial document attacks via sentence-level segmentation and bait-guided context diversity detection, without relying on LLM internal knowledge.

title: Enhancing Noise Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Adaptive Adversarial Training
authors: Feiteng Fang; Yuelin Bai; Shiwen Ni; Min Yang; Xiaojun Chen; Ruifeng Xu
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive adversarial training (RAAT) for RAG noise robustness, categorizes three retrieval noise types (relevant, irrelevant, counterfactual), and introduces RAG-Bench for evaluation.

title: Epistemic Bias Injection: Biasing LLMs via Selective Context Retrieval
authors: Hao Wu; Prateek Saxena
why_relevant: Introduces a novel RAG poisoning attack (Epistemic Bias Injection) using factually correct but biased passages, proposes a defense (BiasDef), and evaluates on a benchmark—directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defenses in RAG.

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
authors: Tianzhe Zhao; Jiaoyan Chen; Shuxiu Zhang; Haiping Zhu; Qika Lin; Jun Liu
why_relevant: Introduces ConflictQA, a benchmark for cross-source knowledge conflicts (text vs KG) in RAG, plus an explanation-based method (XoT) to mitigate evidence bias. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and evaluation under unreliable evidence.

title: Eyes-on-Me: Scalable RAG Poisoning through Transferable Attention-Steering Attractors
authors: Yen-Shan Chen; Sian-Yao Huang; Cheng-Lin Yang; Yun-Nung Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a scalable, transferable RAG poisoning attack via attention-steering attractors, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
authors: Yifei Ming; Senthil Purushwalkam; Shrey Pandit; Zixuan Ke; Xuan-Phi Nguyen; Caiming Xiong; Shafiq Joty
why_relevant: FaithEval is a benchmark specifically targeting contextual faithfulness under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual retrieved contexts—directly aligning with knowledge conflict, OOD/unanswerable, and evaluation aspects of the survey.

title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qinggang Zhang; Zhishang Xiang; Yilin Xiao; Le Wang; Junhui Li; Xinrun Wang; Jinsong Su
why_relevant: Directly addresses parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflicts in RAG, proposing fact-level conflict modeling to improve context faithfulness while analyzing limitations of existing prompting/decoding-based faithful RAG methods.

title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
authors: Yibo Zhao; Jiapeng Zhu; Zichen Ding; Xiang Li
why_relevant: GRACE is an RL framework that jointly trains an RAG model to ground answers in evidence and abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, directly addressing calibration/abstention and unreliable evidence handling.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Grounding

title: Investigating the Factual Knowledge Boundary of Large Language Models with Retrieval Augmentation
authors: Ruiyang Ren; Yuhao Wang; Yingqi Qu; Wayne Xin Zhao; Jing Liu; Hao Tian; Hua Wu; Ji-Rong Wen; Haifeng Wang
why_relevant: Analyzes LLMs' perception of factual knowledge boundaries under retrieval augmentation, including overconfidence, internal-external knowledge conflicts, and dynamic retrieval based on priori/posteriori judgement—directly relevant to calibration, conflict, and when-to-retrieve.

title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights
authors: Yi Chen; Daiwei Chen; Sukrut Madhav Chikodikar; Caitlyn Heqi Yin; Ramya Korlakai Vinayak
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates conformal factuality filtering for RAG, showing fragility under distribution shifts and distractors, and proposes informativeness-aware metrics—directly addressing calibration, robustness, and evaluation of RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Joint-GCG: Unified Gradient-Based Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Haowei Wang; Rupeng Zhang; Junjie Wang; Mingyang Li; Yuekai Huang; Dandan Wang; Qing Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a unified gradient-based corpus poisoning attack jointly optimizing retriever and generator in RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.

title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective
authors: Lu Dai; Liang Sun; Fanpu Cao; Ziyang Rao; Cehao Yang; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
why_relevant: A perspective/survey paper on denoising across the RAG pipeline, covering noise sensitivity, prompt injection, verifiability, and context engineering—directly aligned with the survey's scope.

title: Learning to Filter Context for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhiruo Wang; Jun Araki; Zhengbao Jiang; Md Rizwan Parvez; Graham Neubig
why_relevant: FILCO directly addresses unreliable retrieval by filtering irrelevant/distracting content from retrieved passages before generation, mitigating hallucination caused by noisy context.

title: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
authors: Bowen Jin; Jinsung Yoon; Jiawei Han; Sercan O. Arik
why_relevant: Directly analyzes how hard negatives and noisy retrieved passages degrade long-context RAG and proposes training-free reordering and fine-tuning defenses for robustness.

title: MAGIC: A Multi-Hop and Graph-Based Benchmark for Inter-Context Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jungyeon Lee; Kangmin Lee; Taeuk Kim
why_relevant: Introduces MAGIC, a KG-based benchmark for inter-context knowledge conflicts in RAG, including multi-hop conflicts, directly addressing the conflict and evaluation aspects of the survey.

title: Magic Mushroom: A Customizable Benchmark for Fine-grained Analysis of Retrieval Noise Erosion in RAG Systems
authors: Yuxin Zhang; Yan Wang; Yongrui Chen; Shenyu Zhang; Xinbang Dai; Sheng Bi; Guilin Qi
why_relevant: Introduces a customizable benchmark with fine-grained taxonomy of retrieval noise (distracting, low quality, inconsequential, irrelevant) to evaluate RAG robustness and denoising strategies under varying noise distributions.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
authors: Ori Yoran; Tomer Wolfson; Ori Ram; Jonathan Berant
why_relevant: Directly studies RALM robustness to irrelevant/noisy retrieved context, proposes NLI-based filtering and fine-tuning with mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts, and analyzes failure modes on multiple ODQA benchmarks.

title: NAACL: Noise-AwAre Verbal Confidence Calibration for Robust LLMs in RAG Systems
authors: Jiayu Liu; Rui Wang; Qing Zong; Yumeng Wang; Cheng Qian; Qingcheng Zeng; Tianshi Zheng; Haochen Shi; Dadi Guo; Baixuan Xu; Chunyang Li; Yangqiu Song
why_relevant: Directly studies verbal confidence calibration in RAG under noisy/counterfactual/irrelevant passages, proposing a noise-aware SFT framework and evaluating ECE/AUROC across benchmarks.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control under Noisy Retrieval

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
authors: Xun Xian; Ganghua Wang; Xuan Bi; Jayanth Srinivasa; Ashish Kundu; Charles Fleming; Mingyi Hong; Jie Ding
why_relevant: Proposes universal poisoning attacks against RAG retrieval systems and a detection-based defense, directly addressing adversarial corruption robustness in RAG.

title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Roy Xie; Deepak Gopinath; David Qiu; Dong Lin; Haitian Sun; Saloni Potdar; Bhuwan Dhingra
why_relevant: Studies when search-augmented LLMs should retrieve vs abstain, analyzing over-searching under noisy retrieval, unanswerable/false-premise queries, and multi-turn settings. Introduces TPC metric and OverSearchQA benchmark for evaluating retrieval control and abstention.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve and Abstain

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
authors: Hongyan Chang; Ergute Bao; Xinjian Luo; Ting Yu
why_relevant: Presents an end-to-end indirect prompt injection attack on RAG/agentic systems that solves the retrieval bottleneck via black-box trigger optimization, and evaluates existing defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: POISONCRAFT: Practical Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
authors: Yangguang Shao; Xinjie Lin; Haozheng Luo; Chengshang Hou; Gang Xiong; Jiahao Yu; Junzheng Shi
why_relevant: Proposes a practical query-agnostic poisoning attack against RAG that ensures both retrieval and generation manipulation, and evaluates against defenses—directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.

title: PR-Attack: Coordinated Prompt-RAG Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models via Bilevel Optimization
authors: Yang Jiao; Xiaodong Wang; Kai Yang
why_relevant: Proposes a novel coordinated poisoning + backdoor prompt attack on RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval evidence.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Pengcheng Huang; Zhenghao Liu; Yukun Yan; Haiyan Zhao; Xiaoyuan Yi; Hao Chen; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun; Tong Xiao; Ge Yu; Chenyan Xiong
why_relevant: Directly addresses parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflict by suppressing FFNs linked to unfaithful generation, and introduces CoFaithfulQA benchmark for faithfulness under conflict.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
authors: Baolong Bi; Shenghua Liu; Yiwei Wang; Yilong Xu; Junfeng Fang; Lingrui Mei; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes CK-PLUG, a decoding-time method to control LLM reliance on parametric vs retrieved knowledge using entropy-based confidence gain to detect conflicts, directly addressing knowledge conflict and calibration/control in RAG.

title: Phantom: General Backdoor Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation
authors: Harsh Chaudhari; Giorgio Severi; John Abascal; Anshuman Suri; Matthew Jagielski; Christopher A. Choquette-Choo; Milad Nasr; Cristina Nita-Rotaru; Alina Oprea
why_relevant: Phantom proposes a backdoor poisoning attack on RAG knowledge bases via a single malicious document, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieval-augmented generation.

title: PoisonArena: Uncovering Competing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Liuji Chen; Xiaofang Yang; Yuanzhuo Lu; Jinghao Zhang; Xin Sun; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Jing Dong; Liang Wang
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating competing poisoning attacks on RAG, directly addressing adversarial corruption and conflict among multiple malicious sources. Proposes new competitive evaluation metrics beyond ASR/F1.

title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Wei Zou; Runpeng Geng; Binghui Wang; Jinyuan Jia
why_relevant: PoisonedRAG is the first knowledge corruption/poisoning attack on RAG, directly addressing adversarial corruption of the retrieval knowledge base and evaluating existing defenses.

title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang; Yuxi Chen; Zhuqing Liu; Lihai Nie; Tong Li; Zheli Liu; Minghong Fang
why_relevant: Proposes CorruptRAG, a practical single-text poisoning attack against RAG, and evaluates against multiple defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption robustness.

title: ProGRank: Probe-Gradient Reranking to Defend Dense-Retriever RAG from Corpus Poisoning
authors: Xiangyu Yin; Yi Qi; Chih-Hong Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes a retriever-side, training-free reranking defense against corpus poisoning attacks in dense-retriever RAG, directly addressing adversarial corruption robustness.

title: RAGPart & RAGMask: Retrieval-Stage Defenses Against Corpus Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Pankayaraj Pathmanathan; Michael-Andrei Panaitescu-Liess; Cho-Yu Jason Chiang; Furong Huang
why_relevant: Proposes two retrieval-stage defenses (RAGPart, RAGMask) against corpus poisoning in RAG, evaluated across multiple attacks and retrievers, plus introduces a new attack.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
authors: Zeyu Shen; Basileal Imana; Tong Wu; Chong Xiang; Prateek Mittal; Aleksandra Korolova
why_relevant: Proposes ReliabilityRAG, a provably robust defense against retrieval corpus poisoning/prompt injection in RAG, using MIS over contradiction graphs and reliability-weighted aggregation. Directly addresses adversarial robustness in RAG with empirical and theoretical guarantees.

title: Rescuing the Unpoisoned: Efficient Defense against Knowledge Corruption Attacks on RAG Systems
authors: Minseok Kim; Hankook Lee; Hyungjoon Koo
why_relevant: Proposes RAGDefender, a post-retrieval lightweight defense against knowledge corruption/data poisoning attacks on RAG, with comparative evaluation against RobustRAG and Discern-and-Answer.

title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
authors: Chenyu Lin; Yilin Wen; Du Su; Hexiang Tan; Fei Sun; Muhan Chen; Chenfu Bao; Zhonghou Lyu
why_relevant: Proposes an RL framework (Knowledgeable-R1) that trains LLMs to balance parametric vs contextual knowledge, resisting misleading/counterfactual retrieved context. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and robustness to noisy retrieval.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jingxi Qiu; Zeyu Han; Cheng Huang
why_relevant: SURE-RAG directly addresses evidence sufficiency verification, selective answering/abstention, and uncertainty/conflict signals in RAG, with an artifact-aware evaluation protocol. This aligns with the survey's calibration/control and unreliable-evidence themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Benchmark is constructed (HotpotQA-RAG v3); generalization beyond multi-hop QA is limited.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Selective RAG

title: SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Model
authors: Xun Liang; Simin Niu; Zhiyu Li; Sensen Zhang; Hanyu Wang; Feiyu Xiong; Jason Zhaoxin Fan; Bo Tang; Shichao Song; Mengwei Wang; Jiawei Yang
why_relevant: SafeRAG is a benchmark specifically evaluating RAG vulnerabilities across noise, inter-context conflict, toxicity (soft ad), and DoS attacks, directly aligning with multiple survey axes including adversarial corruption, noisy retrieval, conflict, and evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Chinese-language benchmark; scope limited to news Q&A.

title: Safeguarding RAG Pipelines with GMTP: A Gradient-based Masked Token Probability Method for Poisoned Document Detection
authors: San Kim; Jonghwi Kim; Yejin Jeon; Gary Geunbae Lee
why_relevant: Proposes GMTP, a defense method to detect and filter poisoned documents in RAG knowledge bases by leveraging gradient-based key token identification and masked token probability checks.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
authors: Xiaonan Si; Meilin Zhu; Simeng Qin; Lijia Yu; Lijun Zhang; Shuaitong Liu; Xinfeng Li; Ranjie Duan; Yang Liu; Xiaojun Jia
why_relevant: Proposes a two-stage defense against RAG corpus poisoning with semantic filtering and conflict-aware filtering between internal and external knowledge, directly addressing adversarial corruption and knowledge conflict.

title: Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation against Poisoning Attacks
authors: Zirui Cheng; Jikai Sun; Anjun Gao; Yueyang Quan; Zhuqing Liu; Xiaohua Hu; Minghong Fang
why_relevant: Proposes RAGuard, a detection-based defense against poisoning attacks on RAG using retrieval expansion and perplexity/similarity filtering, evaluated against adaptive attacks.

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hua Ye; Siyuan Chen; Ziqi Zhong; Canran Xiao; Haoliang Zhang; Yuhan Wu; Fei Shen
why_relevant: Proposes a framework for detecting and resolving context-memory conflicts in RAG via interpretable signals (semantic match, factual consistency, self-answerability), directly addressing knowledge conflict and confidence-aware control.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hailey Joren; Jianyi Zhang; Chun-Sung Ferng; Da-Cheng Juan; Ankur Taly; Cyrus Rashtchian
why_relevant: Introduces 'sufficient context' as a lens to analyze RAG errors, stratifying hallucination vs abstention under insufficient evidence, and proposes a selective generation method for guided abstention—directly relevant to calibration, control, and unreliable evidence.

title: Synchronous Faithfulness Monitoring for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Di Wu; Jia-Chen Gu; Fan Yin; Nanyun Peng; Kai-Wei Chang
why_relevant: Proposes a synchronous faithfulness monitor (SynCheck) and faithfulness-oriented decoding to detect and prevent unfaithful RAG outputs, directly addressing context compliance, calibration/abstention, and decoding-time control under unreliable evidence.

title: The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Misleading Information in Long-Context Reasoning
authors: Muhan Gao; Zih-Ching Chen; Kuan-Hao Huang
why_relevant: The paper directly analyzes how hard distractors in long-context RAG degrade performance, providing theoretical and empirical evidence of a nonlinear 'first drop of ink' effect and implications for filtering vs. upstream retrieval precision.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
authors: Yukun Huang; Sanxing Chen; Hongyi Cai; Bhuwan Dhingra
why_relevant: Directly addresses knowledge conflict in RAG by proposing situated faithfulness, with confidence reasoning methods (SCR, RCR) and CR-DPO fine-tuning to calibrate trust between parametric knowledge and external context. Also introduces RedditQA benchmark with naturally occurring incorrect contexts.

title: Toward Robust RALMs: Revealing the Impact of Imperfect Retrieval on Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Seong-Il Park; Jay-Yoon Lee
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates RALM robustness across unanswerable, adversarial, and conflicting retrieval scenarios, introducing a new adversarial attack (GenADV) and robustness metric (RAD).
suggested_section: Evaluation and benchmarks for robust RAG

title: Traceback of Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang; Haoran Xin; Minghong Fang; Zhuqing Liu; Biao Yi; Tong Li; Zheli Liu
why_relevant: Introduces RAGForensics, the first traceback/forensics system to identify poisoned texts in RAG knowledge bases, directly addressing poisoning attacks and defenses central to the survey.

title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
authors: Xi Zhu; Ziqi Wang; Kai Mei; Wujiang Xu; Minghao Guo; Bangji Yang; Jiajun Fan; Dimitris N. Metaxas
why_relevant: Proposes SABER, a self-aware belief estimator for RAG that handles PK-vs-CK knowledge conflict with a 4-cell trust/abstain decision, directly addressing calibration, abstention, and conflict resolution. Also introduces a conflict-QA benchmark with faithfulness metrics.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Huichi Zhou; Kin-Hei Lee; Zhonghao Zhan; Yue Chen; Zhenhao Li; Zhaoyang Wang; Hamed Haddadi; Emine Yilmaz
why_relevant: TrustRAG is a defense framework against corpus poisoning in RAG, using clustering-based filtering and LLM self-assessment to resolve conflicts between internal and external knowledge.

title: Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Zhuoran Jin; Pengfei Cao; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Xiaojian Jiang; Jiexin Xu; Qiuxia Li; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Provides an evaluation framework and analysis of knowledge conflicts in RALMs across internal-vs-external and inter-evidence (truthful/irrelevant/misleading) settings, plus a contrastive decoding method to calibrate model confidence.

title: Typos that Broke the RAG's Back: Genetic Attack on RAG Pipeline by Simulating Documents in the Wild via Low-level Perturbations
authors: Sukmin Cho; Soyeong Jeong; Jeongyeon Seo; Taeho Hwang; Jong C. Park
why_relevant: Proposes GARAG, a genetic black-box adversarial attack injecting low-level typos into retrieval corpora to jointly disrupt retriever and reader in RAG, directly addressing robustness to noisy/adversarial documents.

title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Vinh Nguyen; Cuong Dang; Jiahao Zhang; Hoa Tran; Minh Tran; Trinh Chau; Thai Le; Lu Cheng; Suhang Wang
metadata_topics: rag-core; noisy-retrieval; knowledge-conflict; uncertainty-ood; calibration-control; evaluation-benchmark
why_relevant: URAG is a benchmark explicitly evaluating uncertainty quantification and calibration in RAG systems via conformal prediction, analyzing how retrieval noise, parametric knowledge dependence, and retrieval depth affect confidence and hallucinations.
suggested_section: Evaluation and Benchmarks / Calibration and Uncertainty

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Heydar Soudani; Hamed Zamani; Faegheh Hasibi
why_relevant: Proposes a UQ method for retrieval-augmented reasoning that captures uncertainty from both retriever and generator, and applies it to abstention and model selection—directly relevant to calibration/control and uncertainty under unreliable evidence.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Uncertainty in RAG

title: UniC-RAG: Universal Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Runpeng Geng; Yanting Wang; Ying Chen; Jinyuan Jia
why_relevant: Proposes a universal knowledge corruption (poisoning) attack against RAG, jointly optimizing adversarial texts to compromise thousands of diverse queries, and evaluates existing defenses, directly addressing adversarial robustness of RAG.

title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yikun Han; Mengfei Lan; Halil Kilicoglu
why_relevant: Studies RAG under conflicting biomedical evidence, examining order effects, calibration, and proposing a conflict-aware abstention score. Directly addresses knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and selective prediction.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and uses an existing benchmark.

title: When Safety Becomes a Vulnerability: Exploiting LLM Alignment Homogeneity for Transferable Blocking in RAG
authors: Junchen Li; Chao Qi; Rongzheng Wang; Qizhi Chen; Liang Xu; Di Liang; Bob Simons; Shuang Liang
why_relevant: Proposes TabooRAG, a transferable black-box blocking (denial-of-service) poisoning attack on RAG that exploits safety-alignment homogeneity, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.

title: Why So Gullible? Enhancing the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Models against Counterfactual Noise
authors: Giwon Hong; Jeonghwan Kim; Junmo Kang; Sung-Hyon Myaeng; Joyce Jiyoung Whang
why_relevant: Directly studies robustness of RAG to counterfactual/conflicting retrieved documents, proposes discriminator-based defenses, and releases MacNoise, an LLM-generated conflict benchmark.

title: Why Uncertainty Estimation Methods Fall Short in RAG: An Axiomatic Analysis
authors: Heydar Soudani; Evangelos Kanoulas; Faegheh Hasibi
why_relevant: Provides an axiomatic analysis of uncertainty estimation methods specifically in RAG, showing existing UE methods fail when retrieved context is added, and proposes a calibration function aligned with axioms covering parametric vs non-parametric knowledge interactions.

title: WikiContradict: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Knowledge Conflicts from Wikipedia
authors: Yufang Hou; Alessandra Pascale; Javier Carnerero-Cano; Tigran Tchrakian; Radu Marinescu; Elizabeth Daly; Inkit Padhi; Prasanna Sattigeri
why_relevant: Introduces WikiContradict, a benchmark of real-world inter-context knowledge conflicts from Wikipedia, evaluating how LLMs handle contradictory retrieved passages in RAG settings.

title: Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals
authors: Linda Zeng; Rithwik Gupta; Divij Motwani; Yi Zhang; Diji Yang
why_relevant: Introduces RAGuard, a benchmark using naturally occurring misleading Reddit content to evaluate RAG robustness against misleading/conflicting evidence, showing RAG underperforms zero-shot. Directly relevant to noisy retrieval, conflict, and evaluation themes.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.849/)] Poisoning Retrieval Corpora by Injecting Adversarial Passages
why_relevant: Introduces a corpus poisoning attack on dense retrievers by injecting adversarial passages, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval in RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.96/)] Glue pizza and eat rocks - Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models
why_relevant: Proposes LIAR, a gray-box bi-level attack that injects adversarial documents into RAG knowledge bases to be preferentially retrieved and manipulate LLM output, directly addressing RAG poisoning/injection vulnerabilities.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and injection attacks

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.161/)] Typos that Broke the RAG's Back: Genetic Attack on RAG Pipeline by Simulating Documents in the Wild via Low-level Perturbations
why_relevant: Proposes GARAG, a genetic black-box adversarial attack injecting low-level typo perturbations to jointly disrupt retriever and reader in RAG, demonstrating holistic vulnerability of RAG pipelines to realistic noisy documents.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.801/)] AIP: Subverting Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Adversarial Instructional Prompt
why_relevant: Introduces a novel adversarial attack on RAG via manipulated instructional prompts, exposing a new attack surface beyond query/document poisoning.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13401)] TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes TrojanRAG, a backdoor attack on the retriever component of RAG that manipulates LLM outputs via triggered queries, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Backdoors and Poisoning in RAG

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20485)] Phantom: General Backdoor Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation
why_relevant: Phantom introduces a backdoor poisoning attack on RAG knowledge bases that injects a single malicious document triggered by natural query tokens to induce refusal, bias, exfiltration, and harmful outputs.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00083)] BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: BadRAG introduces corpus poisoning attacks targeting both the retriever (semantic trigger-conditioned backdoor) and downstream LLM generation (DoS, sentiment steering), directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and retrieval backdoors

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10102)] Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
why_relevant: A comprehensive survey of trustworthy RAG covering robustness, factuality, attacks/defenses, and evaluation benchmarks—directly overlapping with the proposed survey's scope.
why_not_or_caveat: As a competing survey, should be cited and differentiated rather than treated as a primary technique.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17275)] On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
why_relevant: Proposes universal poisoning attacks against RAG retrieval systems in knowledge-intensive domains and a detection-based defense, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieval.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: poisoning attacks and defenses

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14050)] GraphRAG under Fire
why_relevant: Presents GRAGPOISON, a novel poisoning attack tailored to GraphRAG, and analyzes why existing RAG poisoning attacks fail on GraphRAG, plus evaluates defenses. Directly addresses adversarial corruption robustness in RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06872)] Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
why_relevant: A comprehensive survey on trustworthy RAG covering reliability (uncertainty, robust generalization), safety (adversarial attacks), privacy, and evaluation—directly overlapping with this survey's scope.
why_not_or_caveat: Broader scope including privacy/fairness/explainability beyond this survey's focus.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19864)] CPA-RAG: Covert Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes CPA-RAG, a covert black-box poisoning attack on RAG that evades perplexity and duplicate-text defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06151)] Joint-GCG: Unified Gradient-Based Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
why_relevant: Proposes Joint-GCG, a gradient-based joint poisoning attack on retriever and generator in RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG systems.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18652)] UniC-RAG: Universal Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a universal knowledge corruption attack injecting adversarial texts into RAG databases to attack diverse queries, and evaluates existing defenses, directly addressing adversarial robustness of RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00586)] Eyes-on-Me: Scalable RAG Poisoning through Transferable Attention-Steering Attractors
why_relevant: Proposes a scalable RAG data poisoning attack using transferable attention-steering attractors, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13842)] ADMIT: Few-shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based Fact Checking
why_relevant: Proposes ADMIT, a few-shot knowledge poisoning attack on RAG-based fact-checking that remains effective even when credible counter-evidence dominates retrieval, and evaluates against multiple defenses.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Y841BRW9rY)] AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
why_relevant: AgentPoison introduces a backdoor poisoning attack against RAG knowledge bases and agent memories, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on LLM agents rather than generic RAG QA, but mechanism is RAG poisoning.

title: \[[ACL](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.610/)\] ATM: Adversarial Tuning Multi-agent System Makes a Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generator
why_relevant: ATM proposes adversarial multi-agent tuning to make RAG generators robust against fabricated/noisy retrieved documents, directly addressing robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: \[[ACL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20978)\] Enhancing Noise Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Adaptive Adversarial Training
why_relevant: Proposes RAAT, an adaptive adversarial training method to enhance LLM robustness against three categorized retrieval noise types (relevant, irrelevant, counterfactual), and introduces RAG-Bench for evaluating noise robustness.

title: \[[ACL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07176v2)\] Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
why_relevant: Astute RAG directly addresses imperfect retrieval and knowledge conflicts by adaptively integrating internal and external knowledge with source-aware consolidation, providing both analysis and a training-free defense method for black-box LLMs.

title: \[[EMNLP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13948)] Typos that Broke the RAG's Back: Genetic Attack on RAG Pipeline by Simulating Documents in the Wild via Low-level Perturbations
why_relevant: Proposes GARAG, a genetic adversarial attack injecting low-level typos to disrupt both retriever and reader in RAG, directly addressing robustness under noisy/adversarial documents.

title: \[[ICLR](https://openreview.net/forum?id=ZS4m74kZpH)\] Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
why_relevant: Directly addresses RALM robustness to irrelevant/noisy retrieved contexts via NLI-based filtering and fine-tuning with mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts, including multi-hop QA.

title: \[[LREC-COLING](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14409)\] Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
why_relevant: Directly investigates knowledge conflicts in RALMs between internal memory and external sources, and among truthful/irrelevant/misleading evidence, plus proposes a contrastive decoding calibration method.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19156)\] Poisoning Retrieval Corpora by Injecting Adversarial Passages
why_relevant: Introduces a corpus poisoning attack that injects adversarial passages into retrieval corpora to mislead dense retrievers, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG evidence.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00396)\] RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
why_relevant: RAGTruth provides a large-scale word-level annotated hallucination corpus specifically for RAG, covering conflicts with retrieved evidence and baseless additions, directly supporting evaluation of robust RAG.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15556)\] Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
why_relevant: Proposes RobustRAG, the first certifiably robust defense against retrieval corruption attacks (PoisonedRAG, indirect prompt injection) via isolate-then-aggregate strategy with secure keyword/decoding aggregation.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00879)\] TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in RAG
why_relevant: TrustRAG is a defense framework against corpus poisoning attacks in RAG, using clustering-based filtering and self-assessment to resolve conflicts between internal and external knowledge.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11400)\] Revisiting Robust RAG: Do We Still Need Complex Robust Training in the Era of Powerful LLMs?
why_relevant: Analyzes robust RAG training methods (RetRobust, RAAT, ATM) against retrieval noise across model scales, examining confidence calibration and attention patterns, directly relevant to noise robustness and calibration discussions.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16101)\] Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals
why_relevant: RAGUARD is a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate RAG robustness against naturally occurring misleading retrievals, with a taxonomy of supporting/misleading/unrelated evidence. It directly targets noisy and conflicting evidence and shows RAG performs worse than zero-shot baselines.
suggested_section: Benchmarks for misleading retrieval and knowledge conflict

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03957)\] Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17118)\] After Retrieval, Before Generation: Enhancing the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in RAG
