title: BalanceRAG: Joint Risk Calibration for Cascaded Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zijun Jia; Yuanchang Ye; Sen Jia; Yiyao Qian; Haoning Wang; Baojie Chen; Diyin Tang; Jinsong Yu; Zhiyuan Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a finite-sample risk-controlled calibration method for cascaded LLM-only/RAG routing with abstention, directly addressing when to retrieve and when to abstain under uncertainty.

title: Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhisheng Qi; Utkarsh Sahu; Li Ma; Haoyu Han; Ryan Rossi; Franck Dernoncourt; Mahantesh Halappanavar; Nesreen Ahmed; Yushun Dong; Yue Zhao; Yu Zhang; Yu Wang
why_relevant: Provides a unified benchmark of knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption and evaluation aspects of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/extraction rather than poisoning or prompt injection, so it covers a narrower slice of adversarial RAG.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Knowledge Conflict for Large Multimodal Models
authors: Yifan Jia; Kailin Jiang; Yuyang Liang; Qihan Ren; Yi Xin; Rui Yang; Fenze Feng; Mingcai Chen; Hengyang Lu; Haozhe Wang; Xiaoye Qu; Dongrui Liu; Lizhen Cui; Yuntao Du
why_relevant: Introduces MMKC-Bench for evaluating context-memory and inter-context knowledge conflicts in multimodal RAG, finding LMMs over-rely on parametric knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Multimodal focus; may be tangential to text-centric RAG sections.

title: Bias Amplification in RAG: Poisoning Knowledge Retrieval to Steer LLMs
authors: Linlin Wang; Tianqing Zhu; Laiqiao Qin; Longxiang Gao; Wanlei Zhou
why_relevant: Proposes a poisoning attack on RAG that amplifies bias via adversarial document injection and subspace projection manipulation of retrieval, plus a dual-stage defense. Relevant to adversarial corruption and defenses in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on fairness/bias amplification rather than factual correctness, a slightly different angle than typical RAG poisoning work.

title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
authors: Hexiang Tan; Fei Sun; Wanli Yang; Yuanzhuo Wang; Qi Cao; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Studies how LLMs resolve conflicts between generated and retrieved contexts, revealing bias toward generated contexts even when incorrect. Directly relevant to retrieved-vs-retrieved/source conflict and context compliance issues in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on generated vs retrieved context conflict rather than classical parametric-vs-retrieved conflict.

title: Bridging External and Parametric Knowledge: Mitigating Hallucination of LLMs with Shared-Private Semantic Synergy in Dual-Stream Knowledge
authors: Yi Sui; Chaozhuo Li; Chen Zhang; Dawei song; Qiuchi Li
why_relevant: Proposes a RAG framework explicitly addressing context-memory and inter-context conflicts, noise filtering of retrieved evidence, and unsupervised hallucination detection to decide when to retrieve.
suggested_section: Knowledge Conflict and Adaptive Retrieval Control

title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
authors: Md Jahedur Rahman; Ihsen Alouani
why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive evasion attack against activation-based prompt injection detectors in RAG settings, and a defense via suffix augmentation. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defenses for RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on detector evasion rather than retrieval pipeline per se, but framed in RAG threat model.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xiaolei Zhang; Xiaojun Jia; Liquan Chen; Songze Li
why_relevant: Proposes a novel corpus-poisoning attack on RAG that injects contradictory documents to induce overthinking in reasoning models, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and knowledge conflict subtopics.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on inference-cost amplification rather than answer correctness, a narrower attack vector.

title: CPA-RAG:Covert Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models
authors: Chunyang Li; Junwei Zhang; Anda Cheng; Zhuo Ma; Xinghua Li; Jianfeng Ma
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box covert poisoning attack on RAG that bypasses defenses like perplexity filtering and duplicate detection, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only paper; limited discussion of defenses.

title: CRAFT: Calibrated Reasoning with Answer-Faithful Traces via Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Hop Question Answering
authors: Yu Liu; Wenxiao Zhang; Diandian Guo; Cong Cao; Fangfang Yuan; Qiang Sun; Yanbing Liu; Jin B. Hong; Zhiyuan Ma
why_relevant: CRAFT addresses right-answer-wrong-reason failures under noisy retrieval in multi-hop RAG via RL with faithfulness/citation rewards, directly targeting robustness, grounding, and auditable reasoning—relevant to noisy retrieval and calibration/control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on faithful reasoning training, not on attacks, conflict resolution, or abstention/confidence calibration in a strict sense.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Faithful Generation under Noisy Retrieval

title: CReSt: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Complex Reasoning over Structured Documents
authors: Minsoo Khang; Sangjun Park; Teakgyu Hong; Dawoon Jung
why_relevant: CReSt is a RAG benchmark that explicitly evaluates refusal behavior under insufficient evidence, citation accuracy, and reasoning over structured documents with negative chunks, touching on uncertainty-awareness and reliability dimensions central to the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Robustness is one of several dimensions; not focused on adversarial or conflict settings.

title: CTRL-RAG: Contrastive Likelihood Reward Based Reinforcement Learning for Context-Faithful RAG Models
authors: Zhehao Tan; Yihan Jiao; Dan Yang; Junjie Wang; Duolin Sun; Jie Feng; Xidong Wang; Lei Liu; Yue Shen; Jian Wang; Jinjie Gu
why_relevant: Proposes an RL training method with contrastive likelihood reward to enforce context faithfulness in RAG, helping models filter noisy documents and ground answers in supporting evidence—directly relevant to knowledge conflict (parametric vs retrieved) and control over context use.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on training/reward design rather than systematic robustness analysis or benchmarking.

title: CUE-R: Beyond the Final Answer in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Siddharth Jain; Venkat Narayan Vedam
why_relevant: Introduces an intervention-based evaluation framework (REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE) measuring per-evidence utility on correctness, grounding, and confidence error in RAG, directly relevant to evaluation under unreliable evidence and calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is evaluation methodology rather than defenses or attacks; suspicious arxiv ID year (2026) suggests verifying provenance.
suggested_section: Evaluation and Metrics for Robust RAG

title: Can LLMs Take Retrieved Information with a Grain of Salt?
authors: Behzad Shayegh; Mohamed Osama Ahmed; Fred Tung; Leo Feng
why_relevant: Proposes a formal metric and interaction strategy for LLMs to adapt RAG outputs to retrieved-context certainty, addressing calibration, uncertainty handling, and prior-vs-context conflict—core themes of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Assumes externally provided certainty scores rather than estimating them; focused on obedience to scores rather than retrieval robustness per se.

title: Can Small Language Models Use What They Retrieve? An Empirical Study of Retrieval Utilization Across Model Scale
authors: Sanchit Pandey
why_relevant: Empirically isolates context utilization failures and distraction effects in small LLMs under oracle and noisy retrieval, directly relevant to distraction and noisy-retrieval robustness analysis.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on small models; diagnostic study rather than proposing defenses.

title: Chain-of-Thought Poisoning Attacks against R1-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hongru Song; Yu-an Liu; Ruqing Zhang; Jiafeng Guo; Yixing Fan
why_relevant: Proposes a novel knowledge base poisoning attack targeting R1-based reasoning RAG systems by wrapping erroneous knowledge in chain-of-thought templates, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrow focus on attack against R1-based systems; no defense proposed.

title: ChunkRAG: Novel LLM-Chunk Filtering Method for RAG Systems
authors: Ishneet Sukhvinder Singh; Ritvik Aggarwal; Ibrahim Allahverdiyev; Muhammad Taha; Aslihan Akalin; Kevin Zhu; Sean O'Brien
why_relevant: ChunkRAG proposes chunk-level LLM filtering to remove irrelevant/weakly related retrieved content, directly targeting noisy retrieval and distraction mitigation in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited evaluation scope (PopQA, PubHealth, Biography); no adversarial or conflict analysis.

title: CoRe-MMRAG: Cross-Source Knowledge Reconciliation for Multimodal RAG
authors: Yang Tian; Fan Liu; Jingyuan Zhang; Victoria W.; Yupeng Hu; Liqiang Nie
why_relevant: Addresses parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge conflict and visual-textual conflict in multimodal RAG, proposing a reconciliation framework to decide which source to trust.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal KB-VQA; not a general robustness study.

title: Confidence-Based Response Abstinence: Improving LLM Trustworthiness via Activation-Based Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Zhiqi Huang; Vivek Datla; Chenyang Zhu; Alfy Samuel; Daben Liu; Anoop Kumar; Ritesh Soni
why_relevant: Proposes activation-based confidence estimation for RAG to enable response abstention, directly addressing calibration and abstain-control under uncertain/ambiguous evidence in production RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (financial customer support) and limited public benchmarking.

title: ConflictRAG: Detecting and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Chenyu Wang; Yingmin Liu; Yang Shu
why_relevant: Proposes a conflict-aware RAG pipeline that detects, classifies, and resolves inter-document and parametric-contextual conflicts, plus a CARS evaluation metric—directly relevant to the knowledge conflict and evaluation themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Suspicious arXiv ID (2605) suggests possible metadata issue; self-constructed benchmark has acknowledged bias.

title: Context Awareness Gate For Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Mohammad Hassan Heydari; Arshia Hemmat; Erfan Naman; Afsaneh Fatemi
why_relevant: Proposes a gating mechanism deciding when to retrieve vs rely on internal knowledge, directly addressing the 'when to retrieve' calibration/control problem and mitigating irrelevant retrieval harms.
why_not_or_caveat: Statistical heuristic with limited evaluation; not a major benchmark.
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve

title: ControlNET: A Firewall for RAG-based LLM System
authors: Hongwei Yao; Haoran Shi; Yidou Chen; Yixin Jiang; Cong Wang; Zhan Qin
why_relevant: Proposes a firewall defense for RAG against poisoning, prompt injection, and data exfiltration attacks, directly addressing adversarial corruption and query flow control.
why_not_or_caveat: Also covers privacy/access-control aspects beyond the survey's core focus on evidence reliability.

title: Copy-Paste to Mitigate Large Language Model Hallucinations
authors: Yongchao Long; Xian Wu; Yingying Zhang; Xianbin Wen; Yuxi Zhou; Shenda Hong
why_relevant: Proposes a training method (CopyPasteLLM) to improve contextual faithfulness under knowledge conflict, addressing the parametric-vs-contextual conflict problem central to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on faithfulness/hallucination mitigation rather than broader robustness like noise or adversarial attacks.

title: CtrlA: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inherent Control
authors: Liu Huanshuo; Hao Zhang; Zhijiang Guo; Jing Wang; Kuicai Dong; Xiangyang Li; Yi Quan Lee; Cong Zhang; Yong Liu
why_relevant: CtrlA addresses when to retrieve in adaptive RAG via honesty steering and confidence monitoring from internal representations, directly relevant to calibration/control over retrieval triggering.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
authors: Zhuoran Jin; Pengfei Cao; Hongbang Yuan; Yubo Chen; Jiexin Xu; Huaijun Li; Xiaojian Jiang; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Interprets the mechanism of knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and external context, and proposes attention-head pruning to control whether LMs follow internal memory or retrieved context—directly relevant to the conflict and control axes of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on mechanistic interpretability on a controlled factual recall task rather than full RAG pipelines.

title: D$^2$Plan: Dual-Agent Dynamic Global Planning for Complex Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Kangcheng Luo; Tinglang Wu; Yansong Feng
why_relevant: Proposes a dual-agent planning method to mitigate distraction by irrelevant retrieved evidence and ineffective query construction in multi-hop RAG, with a Purifier explicitly filtering noisy retrievals and adaptive re-retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multi-hop QA performance rather than systematic robustness analysis or calibration.

title: DYNAMICQA: Tracing Internal Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
authors: Sara Vera Marjanović; Haeun Yu; Pepa Atanasova; Maria Maistro; Christina Lioma; Isabelle Augenstein
why_relevant: Introduces DynamicQA, a benchmark for studying intra-memory and context-memory knowledge conflicts with realistic temporal/disputable facts, directly relevant to RAG's struggle with conflicting evidence and parametric vs. contextual knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is more on intra-memory conflict and semantic entropy than on retrieval pipeline robustness per se.

title: Data Extraction Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoors
authors: Yuefeng Peng; Junda Wang; Hong Yu; Amir Houmansadr
why_relevant: Proposes backdoor-based data extraction attacks against RAG systems, contributing to the adversarial corruption threat model including poisoning and privacy leakage.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/extraction rather than answer-quality robustness; tangential to calibration/conflict aspects.

title: DeRAG: Black-box Adversarial Attacks on Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications via Prompt Injection
authors: Jerry Wang; Fang Yu
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box differential evolution attack that injects adversarial suffixes to manipulate RAG retrieval rankings, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses solely on attack methodology without defense or calibration discussion.

title: Decide Then Retrieve: A Training-Free Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Triggering and Dual-Path Retrieval
authors: Wang Chen; Guanqiang Qi; Weikang Li; Yang Li; Deguo Xia; Jizhou Huang
why_relevant: Proposes uncertainty-guided adaptive retrieval triggering and dual-path evidence selection to mitigate retrieval noise, directly addressing when-to-retrieve calibration and noisy retrieval issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA performance; does not address adversarial or conflict settings.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Deep Search with Hierarchical Meta-Cognitive Monitoring Inspired by Cognitive Neuroscience
authors: Zhongxiang Sun; Qipeng Wang; Weijie Yu; Jingxuan Yang; Haolang Lu; Jun Xu
why_relevant: Proposes a metacognitive monitoring framework for deep search agents that detects abnormal reasoning/retrieval states using consistency between searching entropy and reasoning entropy, and triggers corrective intervention—directly addressing calibration, control, and when-to-intervene under uncertainty in RAG-like agents.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on deep search agents rather than canonical RAG; robustness framing is broad rather than specifically targeting noise/conflict/adversarial settings.

title: DeepEra: A Deep Evidence Reranking Agent for Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated Question Answering
authors: Haotian Chen; Qingqing Long; Siyu Pu; Xiao Luo; Wei Ju; Meng Xiao; Yuanchun Zhou; Jianghua Zhao; Xuezhi Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a reranking agent and benchmark (SciRAG-SSLI) specifically targeting semantically similar but logically irrelevant distractor passages in RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on scientific QA domain; reranking-centric rather than full robustness taxonomy.

title: Defending Against Knowledge Poisoning Attacks During Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu; Vinay M. Shashidhar; Micheal Tuape; Dan Abudu; Beakcheol Jang; Jong Wook Kim
why_relevant: Proposes filtration-based defenses (FilterRAG, ML-FilterRAG) against PoisonedRAG knowledge poisoning attacks, directly addressing adversarial corruption of RAG knowledge bases.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrowly targets PoisonedRAG-style attacks; relies on a specific statistical property.

title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
authors: Tongyu Wen; Chenglong Wang; Xiyuan Yang; Haoyu Tang; Yueqi Xie; Lingjuan Lyu; Zhicheng Dou; Fangzhao Wu
why_relevant: Proposes a detection-based defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG using LLM hidden states/gradients, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved content.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection

title: Defense Against Prompt Injection Attack by Leveraging Attack Techniques
authors: Yulin Chen; Haoran Li; Zihao Zheng; Yangqiu Song; Dekai Wu; Bryan Hooi
why_relevant: Proposes training-free defenses against indirect prompt injection attacks, including those embedded in retrieved content, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG inputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is general prompt injection rather than RAG-specific poisoning, but indirect injection via retrieved data is a key threat model.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against prompt injection

title: Dialectical Alignment: Resolving the Tension of 3H and Security Threats of LLMs
authors: Shu Yang; Jiayuan Su; Han Jiang; Mengdi Li; Keyuan Cheng; Muhammad Asif Ali; Lijie Hu; Di Wang
why_relevant: Proposes alignment-based defense against poisoned context attacks in RAG while balancing context-memory and inter-context conflicts, directly addressing knowledge conflict and adversarial corruption.

title: Do Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Adapt to Varying User Needs?
authors: Peilin Wu; Xinlu Zhang; Wenhao Yu; Xingyu Liu; Xinya Du; Zhiyu Zoey Chen
why_relevant: Introduces an evaluation framework assessing RALMs across user-instruction modes (Context-Exclusive/First, Memory-First) under context matching, knowledge conflict, and irrelevant retrieval, directly addressing conflict resolution, instruction compliance, and robustness to noisy context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on user-need adaptation rather than novel defenses; adversarial coverage is limited to counterfactual context.

title: Does RAG Know When Retrieval Is Wrong? Diagnosing Context Compliance under Knowledge Conflict
authors: Yihang Chen; Pin Qian; Su Wang; Sipeng Zhang; Huan Xu; Shuhuai Lin; Xinpeng Wei
why_relevant: Proposes a diagnostic (CDD) and benchmark (Epi-Scale) for context-compliance under context-memory knowledge conflict, including temporal drift and distractor evidence, directly relevant to conflict and distraction subtopics.
why_not_or_caveat: Suspicious arXiv ID (2605.xxxx) and 2026 date suggest possible preprint anomaly; authors not claiming a deployment method.

title: Don't Hallucinate, Abstain: Identifying LLM Knowledge Gaps via Multi-LLM Collaboration
authors: Shangbin Feng; Weijia Shi; Yike Wang; Wenxuan Ding; Vidhisha Balachandran; Yulia Tsvetkov
why_relevant: Proposes methods to identify LLM knowledge gaps and abstain from answering, directly relevant to calibration/abstention. Also analyzes retrieval augmentation failure cases.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is primarily on LLM abstention rather than RAG specifically; RAG analysis is secondary.

title: Dynamic Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Mitigating Distractors and Positional Bias
authors: Malika Iratni; Mohand Boughanem; Taoufiq Dkaki
why_relevant: Analyzes distractor impact and positional bias in RAG, and proposes a classifier to dynamically select retrieval size, directly addressing distraction and adaptive retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited to MuSiQue and a simple classifier; not a foundational work.

title: END: Early Noise Dropping for Efficient and Effective Context Denoising
authors: Hongye Jin; Pei Chen; Jingfeng Yang; Zhengyang Wang; Fangran Mo; Jinghan Zhang; Meng Jiang; Yifan Gao; Binxuan Huang; Xinyang Zhang; Zheng Li; Tianyi Liu; Huasheng Li; Bing Yin
why_relevant: Proposes a method to detect and drop noisy/distracting chunks in RAG and long-context inputs using early-layer probers, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on efficiency-aware denoising rather than adversarial or conflict settings.

title: Efficient OpAmp Adaptation for Zoom Attention to Golden Contexts
authors: Haoyuan Wu; Rui Ming; Haisheng Zheng; Zhuolun He; Bei Yu
why_relevant: Proposes an attention adaptation method to mitigate distraction from noisy retrieved documents in RAG, directly targeting the problem of LLMs allocating attention to irrelevant contexts instead of the golden document.
why_not_or_caveat: Architectural method rather than retrieval-side robustness; evaluation focuses on noisy-context QA benchmarks.

title: Eliciting Critical Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models via Contrastive Explanations
authors: Leonardo Ranaldi; Marco Valentino; Andrè Freitas
why_relevant: Proposes Contrastive-RAG to elicit critical reasoning over retrieved passages, explicitly evaluating robustness to noisy/shuffled documents and discriminating relevant vs irrelevant evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompting/distillation method rather than systematic robustness analysis.

title: Energy Landscapes Enable Reliable Abstention in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Healthcare
authors: Ravi Shankar; Sheng Wong; Lin Li; Magdalena Bachmann; Alex Silverthorne; Beth Albert; Gabriel Davis Jones
why_relevant: Proposes an energy-based abstention mechanism for RAG that detects OOD/near-distribution queries and triggers abstention, directly addressing calibration, uncertainty, and when-not-to-answer control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (women's health) and focuses on query-level OOD rather than retrieved-evidence robustness.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with In-Context Learning
authors: Seong-Il Park; Seung-Woo Choi; Na-Hyun Kim; Jay-Yoon Lee
why_relevant: Proposes in-context learning with MRC and conflict demonstrations to make RALMs more robust to unanswerable queries and conflicting retrieved contexts, directly addressing noisy retrieval and knowledge conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Method is relatively lightweight; experiments limited to NQ and WebQ.

title: Entropy-Based Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Zexuan Qiu; Zijing Ou; Bin Wu; Jingjing Li; Aiwei Liu; Irwin King
why_relevant: Proposes an entropy-based decoding method to mitigate distraction from noisy retrieved documents and conflicts with parametric knowledge in RAG, directly addressing robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: EviNote-RAG: Enhancing RAG Models via Answer-Supportive Evidence Notes
authors: Yuqin Dai; Guoqing Wang; Yuan Wang; Kairan Dou; Kaichen Zhou; Zhanwei Zhang; Shuo Yang; Fei Tang; Jun Yin; Pengyu Zeng; Zhenzhe Ying; Can Yi; Changhua Meng; Yuchen Zhou; Yongliang Shen; Shuai Lu
why_relevant: EviNote-RAG explicitly addresses low signal-to-noise ratio in retrieved evidence and error accumulation in multi-hop reasoning by generating supportive-evidence notes with an entailment-based reward, directly relevant to noise robustness in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on noise filtering via summarization; does not address conflict, adversarial, or calibration aspects.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Knowledge Base Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Bo Lin; Shangwen Wang; Liqian Chen; Xiaoguang Mao
why_relevant: First empirical study of knowledge base poisoning in retrieval-augmented code generation, showing that vulnerable code injected into the KB propagates security issues into generated code. Directly relevant to the adversarial corruption / poisoning subsection of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation rather than general QA RAG.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Retriever Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Tian Li; Bo Lin; Shangwen Wang; Yusong Tan
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy backdoor attack on the retriever component in retrieval-augmented code generation, demonstrating a new supply-chain threat vector against RAG and evading existing defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation, but the retriever-backdoor threat model is broadly relevant to RAG robustness.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Retrieval Attacks and Backdoors

title: FVA-RAG: Falsification-Verification Alignment for Mitigating Sycophantic Hallucinations
authors: Mayank Ravishankara
why_relevant: Addresses retrieval sycophancy (premise-confirming bias) by explicitly retrieving counter-evidence and adjudicating contradictions, directly tackling reliability under misleading retrieved context.
why_not_or_caveat: Independent preprint with limited evaluation (TruthfulQA only) and prompted baselines rather than original fine-tuned Self-RAG/CRAG.

title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
authors: Passant Elchafei; Monorama Swain; Shahed Masoudian; Markus Schedl
why_relevant: Introduces a facet-level diagnostic framework that traces evidence uncertainty and retrieval-generation misalignment in RAG, characterizing failure modes such as evidence absence, misalignment, and parametric-knowledge overrides. Directly relevant to knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and evaluation of RAG faithfulness.
why_not_or_caveat: Diagnostic/analysis rather than a defense or new method; limited datasets.
suggested_section: Evaluation and Diagnostics of Evidence Usage

title: Fact or Facsimile? Evaluating the Factual Robustness of Modern Retrievers
authors: Haoyu Wu; Qingcheng Zeng; Kaize Ding
why_relevant: Analyzes factual robustness of dense retrievers/rerankers used in RAG, showing vulnerability to distractors and paraphrase-based perturbations, with implications for RAG poisoning attack surface.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retriever component factuality rather than end-to-end RAG behavior.

title: Fact-Checking with Large Language Models via Probabilistic Certainty and Consistency
authors: Haoran Wang; Maryam Khalid; Qiong Wu; Jian Gao; Cheng Cao
why_relevant: Proposes a confidence-based adaptive routing mechanism deciding when to rely on parametric knowledge vs trigger retrieval/deep search, directly addressing calibration and control of retrieval under uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on fact-checking rather than general RAG QA; robustness to noisy/adversarial evidence not the central concern.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Ekaterina Fadeeva; Aleksandr Rubashevskii; Dzianis Piatrashyn; Roman Vashurin; Shehzaad Dhuliawala; Artem Shelmanov; Timothy Baldwin; Preslav Nakov; Mrinmaya Sachan; Maxim Panov
why_relevant: Proposes FRANQ, a faithfulness-aware uncertainty quantification method to detect factual errors in RAG outputs, distinguishing between hallucinations from retrieval grounding vs. parametric knowledge. Directly relevant to calibration and conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge.

title: Faithfulness-QA: A Counterfactual Entity Substitution Dataset for Training Context-Faithful RAG Models
authors: Li Ju; Junzhe Wang; Qi Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces a large counterfactual entity substitution dataset to train and evaluate RAG models for context-faithfulness under context-vs-parametric knowledge conflicts.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a dataset construction paper without new modeling or extensive empirical analysis.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Zhenting Qi; Hanlin Zhang; Eric Xing; Sham Kakade; Himabindu Lakkaraju
why_relevant: Demonstrates prompt-injection data extraction attacks against RAG datastores, exposing a privacy/adversarial vulnerability relevant to robustness against malicious inputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on datastore privacy leakage rather than evidence-corruption attacks affecting answer reliability.

title: From Facts to Conclusions : Integrating Deductive Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
authors: Shubham Mishra; Samyek Jain; Gorang Mehrishi; Shiv Tiwari; Harsh Sharma; Pratik Narang; Dhruv Kumar
why_relevant: Proposes a reasoning-trace-augmented RAG framework explicitly for handling conflicting/outdated evidence with justified refusals, and introduces a Conflict-Aware Trust Score (CATS) evaluation metric covering groundedness, refusal, and conflict-behavior alignment.
why_not_or_caveat: Small 539-query dataset and reliance on LLM-as-judge limits generality.

title: Generate, Discriminate, Evolve: Enhancing Context Faithfulness via Fine-Grained Sentence-Level Self-Evolution
authors: Kun Li; Tianhua Zhang; Yunxiang Li; Hongyin Luo; Abdalla Moustafa; Xixin Wu; James Glass; Helen Meng
why_relevant: Proposes a self-evolving framework to enhance context faithfulness in RAG, directly addressing knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and retrieved evidence via sentence-level optimization.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on faithfulness training rather than broader robustness; evaluated only on ASQA/ConFiQA.

title: Generating Leakage-Free Benchmarks for Robust RAG Evaluation
authors: Jiayi Liu; Jiaxing Zhang; Bowen Jin; Jennifer Neville
why_relevant: Proposes a leakage-free benchmark generation pipeline to isolate retrieval quality from parametric memory, directly addressing evaluation reliability and parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge issues in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on benchmark construction rather than robustness mechanisms per se.

title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi; Aideen Fay; Giovanni Cherubin; Ahmed Salem; Mario Fritz; Andrew Paverd
why_relevant: Proposes activation-delta probing to detect indirect prompt injection (task drift) in retrieval-augmented LLMs, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on prompt injection detection generally rather than RAG-specific retrieval pipeline robustness.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against indirect prompt injection

title: Grounded Decoding: Retrieval-Anchored Probability Fusion for Faithful RAG
authors: Ibne Farabi Shihab; Fariya Afrin; Sanjeda Akter; Anuj Sharma
why_relevant: Proposes a decoding-time method to enforce grounding in retrieved evidence over parametric knowledge, with adaptive weighting based on distributional conflict and retriever confidence—directly relevant to knowledge conflict and control.

title: Guaranteeing Knowledge Integration with Joint Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhengyi Zhao; Shubo Zhang; Zezhong Wang; Yuxi Zhang; Huimin Wang; Yutian Zhao; Yefeng Zheng; Binyang Li; Kam-Fai Wong; Xian Wu
why_relevant: Directly addresses parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflict via dual-path decoding and contrastive DPO, with an adaptive retrieval decision module.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on integration method rather than systematic robustness evaluation; suspicious arxiv ID (future-dated).

title: Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents
authors: Sidharth Pulipaka; Stanislau Hlebik; Leonidas Raghav; Sahar Abdelnabi; Vyas Raina; Ivaxi Sheth; Mario Fritz
why_relevant: Studies indirect prompt injection that poisons persistent memory of LLM agents, causing delayed retrieval-driven malicious behavior. Relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval/memory stores in RAG-like pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on agent memory rather than classic RAG corpora; relevance is via analogy to retrieval poisoning and indirect injection.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection

title: Hidden in the Metadata: Stealth Poisoning Attacks on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu; Mohammad Mahdi Shokri
why_relevant: Presents a stealth metadata-only poisoning attack against multimodal RAG, evaluates defenses, and exposes retrieval vulnerabilities—directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG; narrower scope than general text RAG poisoning.

title: Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG
authors: Haoze Guo; Ziqi Wei
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark and harness for evaluating indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning in web-facing RAG, with defenses (sanitization, normalization, attribution-gating) and metrics (ASR, ΔMRR, ΔnDCG).
why_not_or_caveat: Short workshop-style paper; narrow focus on social-web carriers.

title: Hit-RAG: Learning to Reason with Long Contexts via Preference Alignment
authors: Junming Liu; Yuqi Li; Shiping Wen; Zhigang Zeng; Tingwen Huang
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-stage preference alignment framework to harden MLLMs against noisy distractors and reasoning collapse in long-context RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal long-context RAG; suspicious arxiv id (2603) suggests possible metadata issue.

title: How Confident Is the First Token? An Uncertainty-Calibrated Prompt Optimization Framework for Large Language Model Classification and Understanding
authors: Wei Chen; Guoyang Ju; Yuanyuan Qi
why_relevant: Proposes a first-token uncertainty metric (LSFU) used to adaptively trigger RAG only for high-uncertainty samples, directly addressing when-to-retrieve and confidence calibration—core topics of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on classification tasks rather than open-domain QA; RAG robustness is a secondary motivation.

title: How Does Knowledge Selection Help Retrieval Augmented Generation?
authors: Xiangci Li; Jessica Ouyang
why_relevant: Empirically analyzes how knowledge selection (reranking/filtering) and the mix of gold vs distractor passages affect RAG generation quality, directly informing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on selection/recall trade-offs rather than adversarial or conflict settings.

title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions
authors: Shuowei Li; Haoxin Li; Wenda Chu; Yi Fang
why_relevant: Proposes a three-source (parametric, user, document) interaction framework to study knowledge conflict and models' ability to discriminate helpful vs misleading external information, directly relevant to conflict and context compliance.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader than RAG (includes user sycophancy), not specifically about retrieval pipelines.

title: How Retrieved Context Shapes Internal Representations in RAG
authors: Samuel Yeh; Sharon Li
why_relevant: Analyzes how relevant, distracting, and random retrieved documents shape LLM internal representations and downstream behavior in RAG, connecting noise/distraction to abstention and parametric-vs-retrieved interactions.
why_not_or_caveat: Representation-level analysis rather than a new robustness method or benchmark.

title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
authors: Che Wang; Fuyao Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Ziqi Zhang; Yinghui Wang; Longtao Huang; Jianbo Gao; Zhong Chen; Wei Yang Bryan Lim
why_relevant: Proposes an inference-time defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in tool-augmented LLM agents, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved content in RAG-style settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent tool-use rather than classical RAG QA; relevance to retrieval robustness is via IPI in retrieved content.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses

title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Alexandra Bazarova; Andrei Volodichev; Daria Kotova; Alexey Zaytsev
why_relevant: Proposes a mechanistically grounded uncertainty quantification method for RAG to detect hallucinations, directly addressing calibration and confidence estimation under retrieval grounding.

title: ImportSnare: Directed "Code Manual" Hijacking in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Kai Ye; Liangcai Su; Chenxiong Qian
why_relevant: Presents a novel RAG poisoning attack targeting retrieval-augmented code generation, manipulating both retrieval ranking and LLM generation to recommend malicious dependencies, with a released benchmark.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation rather than general RAG QA.

title: Improving Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Language Models through Dialectic Reasoning Argumentations
authors: Leonardo Ranaldi; Federico Ranaldi; Fabio Massimo Zanzotto; Barry Haddow; Alexandra Birch
why_relevant: Proposes a dialectic reasoning RAG framework that handles conflicting/irrelevant multilingual retrieved evidence and shows robustness to misleading retrieval and reranking perturbations.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multilingual RAG reasoning rather than dedicated robustness study; robustness experiments are secondary.
suggested_section: Knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval mitigation

title: InterpDetect: Interpretable Signals for Detecting Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Likun Tan; Kuan-Wei Huang; Joy Shi; Kevin Wu
why_relevant: Proposes mechanistic detection of RAG hallucinations by disentangling parametric vs external knowledge contributions, directly addressing knowledge conflict and reliability monitoring in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on detection via interpretability signals rather than mitigation; evaluated on FinQA only.

title: Investigating Context-Faithfulness in Large Language Models: The Roles of Memory Strength and Evidence Style
authors: Yuepei Li; Kang Zhou; Qiao Qiao; Bach Nguyen; Qing Wang; Qi Li
why_relevant: Analyzes context faithfulness of LLMs under knowledge conflicts, quantifying memory strength and the effect of evidence style on receptiveness to retrieved evidence.

title: Investigating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems on Unanswerable, Uncheatable, Realistic, Multi-hop Queries
authors: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu; Bryan Li; Arman Cohan; William Gantt Walden; Eugene Yang
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark pipeline for unanswerable, multi-hop RAG queries, testing systems' ability to reject out-of-scope queries and identify retrieval/reasoning failures—directly relevant to OOD/uncertainty and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on benchmark construction rather than methods for robustness or calibration.

title: Investigating the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation at the Query Level
authors: Sezen Percin; Xin Su; Qutub Sha Syed; Phillip Howard; Aleksei Kuvshinov; Leo Schwinn; Kay-Ulrich Scholl
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates RAG pipeline robustness to query-level perturbations (typos, redundancy, tone, ambiguity), measuring component-wise sensitivity across retrievers and LLMs, which fits noisy-input robustness and evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on query perturbations rather than evidence corruption; tangential to conflict/adversarial themes.
suggested_section: Evaluation and robustness to input perturbations

title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance
authors: Eunbyeol Cho; Yunseung Lee; Mirae Kim; Jeewon Yang; Youngjun Kwak; Edward Choi
why_relevant: Introduces a multi-turn RAG hallucination detection benchmark with a taxonomy covering contradictions, unverifiable claims, irrelevance, and justified abstention—directly relevant to evaluating RAG robustness, context faithfulness, and refusal calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (Korean finance), which may limit generality.

title: KEPo: Knowledge Evolution Poison on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qizhi Chen; Chao Qi; Yihong Huang; Muquan Li; Rongzheng Wang; Dongyang Zhang; Ke Qin; Shuang Liang
why_relevant: Proposes a novel poisoning attack tailored to GraphRAG, exposing vulnerabilities specific to graph-based retrieval-augmented generation.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: Know Or Not: a library for evaluating out-of-knowledge base robustness
authors: Jessica Foo; Pradyumna Shyama Prasad; Shaun Khoo
why_relevant: Provides a methodology and open-source library plus PolicyBench benchmark for evaluating out-of-knowledge-base robustness in RAG, focusing on abstention when retrieved context is insufficient.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrowly scoped to OOKB abstention evaluation; does not address adversarial or conflict scenarios.

title: Know When You're Wrong: Aligning Confidence with Correctness for LLM Error Detection
authors: Xie Xiaohu; Liu Xiaohu; Yao Benjamin
why_relevant: Proposes a normalized confidence score and self-evaluation for LLM error detection, with direct application to adaptive RAG (selective retrieval when uncertain). Also analyzes calibration impacts of SFT/RL/DPO and proposes a fix.
why_not_or_caveat: Adaptive RAG is a demonstration rather than the primary focus; broader scope is general LLM calibration.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: KnowPO: Knowledge-aware Preference Optimization for Controllable Knowledge Selection in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Ruizhe Zhang; Yongxin Xu; Yuzhen Xiao; Runchuan Zhu; Xinke Jiang; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a preference optimization approach for balancing adherence to retrieved context and robustness to noise under knowledge conflicts, directly addressing context vs parametric conflicts and noisy retrieval.

title: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Medical Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Peiru Yang; Haoran Zheng; Tong Ju; Shiting Wang; Wanchun Ni; Jiajun Liu; Shangguang Wang; Yongfeng Huang; Tao Qi
why_relevant: Proposes a query-agnostic knowledge poisoning attack on medical multimodal RAG, targeting both retrieval hijacking and generation manipulation, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical multimodal); attack-only, no defense.

title: LLM-Independent Adaptive RAG: Let the Question Speak for Itself
authors: Maria Marina; Nikolay Ivanov; Sergey Pletenev; Mikhail Salnikov; Daria Galimzianova; Nikita Krayko; Vasily Konovalov; Alexander Panchenko; Viktor Moskvoretskii
why_relevant: Proposes LLM-independent adaptive retrieval using external features to decide when to retrieve, directly addressing the calibration/control axis of robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on efficiency of retrieval-trigger decisions rather than robustness to noisy or adversarial evidence.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: LLMail-Inject: A Dataset from a Realistic Adaptive Prompt Injection Challenge
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi; Aideen Fay; Ahmed Salem; Egor Zverev; Kai-Chieh Liao; Chi-Huang Liu; Chun-Chih Kuo; Jannis Weigend; Danyael Manlangit; Alex Apostolov; Haris Umair; João Donato; Masayuki Kawakita; Athar Mahboob; Tran Huu Bach; Tsun-Han Chiang; Myeongjin Cho; Hajin Choi; Byeonghyeon Kim; Hyeonjin Lee; Benjamin Pannell; Conor McCauley; Mark Russinovich; Andrew Paverd; Giovanni Cherubin
why_relevant: Provides a large-scale dataset and analysis of adaptive indirect prompt injection attacks against an LLM-based email assistant with retrieval, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defenses in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on prompt injection in agentic email setting rather than general RAG poisoning.

title: LatentAudit: Real-Time White-Box Faithfulness Monitoring for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Verifiable Deployment
authors: Zhe Yu; Wenpeng Xing; Meng Han
why_relevant: Proposes a real-time faithfulness monitor for RAG that flags unsupported answers under contradictions, retrieval misses, and partial-support noise, directly relevant to calibration/abstention and robustness to unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus on internal-state monitoring and verifiable deployment; zk-proof aspect is tangential to the survey.

title: Learning to Trust: Dynamic Utilization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for E-commerce Search Relevance
authors: Tingqiao Xu; Shaowei Yao; Chenhe Dong; Yiming Jin; Zerui Huang; Dan Ou; Haihong Tang; Bo Zheng
why_relevant: Proposes an RL framework teaching LLMs to dynamically trust or ignore noisy retrieved context, directly addressing knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence and context-trust calibration in a production RAG setting.
why_not_or_caveat: Application-focused on e-commerce search relevance; evaluation is industry-specific rather than on standard robustness benchmarks.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Dynamic Context Utilization

title: Lessons from Training Grounded LLMs with Verifiable Rewards
authors: Shang Hong Sim; Tej Deep Pala; Vernon Toh; Hai Leong Chieu; Amir Zadeh; Chuan Li; Navonil Majumder; Soujanya Poria
why_relevant: Trains RAG LLMs with verifiable rewards for citation grounding and refusal on unanswerable queries, directly addressing abstention and grounded generation under unreliable/insufficient evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus on training method rather than benchmarking robustness; doesn't address adversarial or conflict scenarios.

title: LogicPoison: Logical Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yilin Xiao; Jin Chen; Qinggang Zhang; Yujing Zhang; Chuang Zhou; Longhao Yang; Lingfei Ren; Xin Yang; Xiao Huang
why_relevant: Proposes a novel poisoning attack against GraphRAG that corrupts logical/topological structure, expanding the adversarial corruption taxonomy beyond text injection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused specifically on GraphRAG variant; no defense proposed.

title: Look It Up: Analysing Internal Web Search Capabilities of Modern LLMs
authors: Sahil Kale
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark assessing when LLMs decide to invoke web search vs rely on parametric knowledge, measuring confidence calibration, selective retrieval, and accuracy gains—directly relevant to calibration/control of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on commercial models' built-in web search rather than general RAG pipelines; limited to factual QA.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: MIPIAD: Multilingual Indirect Prompt Injection Attack Defense with Qwen -- TF-IDF Hybrid and Meta-Ensemble Learning
authors: Al Muhit Muhtadi; Mostafa Rifat Tazwar
why_relevant: Proposes a multilingual defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG/tool-using LLMs and provides a large benchmark built on BIPIA, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption axis of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on input classification rather than RAG pipeline integration; empirical scope limited to English and Bangla.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses

title: MM-PoisonRAG: Disrupting Multimodal RAG with Local and Global Poisoning Attacks
authors: Hyeonjeong Ha; Qiusi Zhan; Jeonghwan Kim; Dimitrios Bralios; Saikrishna Sanniboina; Nanyun Peng; Kai-Wei Chang; Daniel Kang; Heng Ji
why_relevant: Introduces localized and globalized poisoning attacks against multimodal RAG, demonstrating cross-modal knowledge base vulnerabilities and bypass of existing defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG, narrower than text-only RAG poisoning.

title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
authors: Junhyeok Lee; Han Jang; Kyu Sung Choi
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark for direct and indirect (RAG-mediated) prompt injection in clinical settings, with outcome-based metrics distinguishing instruction compliance from downstream harm. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and evaluation of robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (clinical), so its generality to broader robust-RAG evaluation is limited.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: indirect prompt injection benchmarks

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
authors: Sara Rosenthal; Yannis Katsis; Vraj Shah; Lihong He; Lucian Popa; Marina Danilevsky
why_relevant: MTRAG-UN benchmarks multi-turn RAG on unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and unclear responses, directly probing abstention, clarification, and handling of ambiguous/unsupported queries.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-turn conversational challenges rather than adversarial or noisy retrieval per se.
suggested_section: Evaluation/benchmarks for OOD, abstention, and clarification

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
authors: Saksham Sahai Srivastava; Haoyu He
why_relevant: Introduces a memory-poisoning attack on agentic RAG long-term memory, exploiting semantic retrieval to induce persistent behavioral drift. Relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval stores.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent memory rather than canonical RAG knowledge base poisoning; narrow validation on MetaGPT.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and memory attacks

title: Merging Generated and Retrieved Knowledge for Open-Domain QA
authors: Yunxiang Zhang; Muhammad Khalifa; Lajanugen Logeswaran; Moontae Lee; Honglak Lee; Lu Wang
why_relevant: Proposes COMBO to resolve conflicts between LLM-generated and retrieved passages, directly addressing knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on parametric-vs-retrieved conflict in ODQA; not on adversarial or noisy retrieval per se.

title: Micro-Act: Mitigating Knowledge Conflict in LLM-based RAG via Actionable Self-Reasoning
authors: Nan Huo; Jinyang Li; Bowen Qin; Ge Qu; Xiaolong Li; Xiaodong Li; Chenhao Ma; Reynold Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes Micro-Act, an ICL-based method to mitigate parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge conflicts via fine-grained decomposition, evaluated across multiple conflict types and preserving performance in conflict-free cases.

title: Modeling Uncertainty Trends for Timely Retrieval in Dynamic RAG
authors: Bo Li; Tian Tian; Zhenghua Xu; Hao Cheng; Shikun Zhang; Wei Ye
why_relevant: Proposes an uncertainty-trend-based method for deciding when to retrieve in dynamic RAG, directly addressing calibration/control of retrieval timing using entropy-based uncertainty signals.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retrieval timing rather than handling unreliable evidence per se.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Modeling Uncertainty and Using Post-fusion as Fallback Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLMs
authors: Ye Liu; Semih Yavuz; Rui Meng; Meghana Moorthy; Shafiq Joty; Caiming Xiong; Yingbo Zhou
why_relevant: Studies how LLMs fail to use retrieved passages even when correct evidence is present, modeling 'unknown' outputs as uncertainty and proposing fallback fusion strategies. Directly addresses calibration/abstention and noisy-retrieval integration in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on single-hop QA with limited adversarial/conflict scope.

title: Needle-in-RAG: Prompt-Conditioned Character-Level Traceback of Poisoned Spans in Retrieved Evidence
authors: Huining Cui; Wei Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a forensic traceback framework for character-level localization of poisoned spans in RAG retrieved evidence, with an evaluation protocol across five poisoning attack families and six LLMs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on post-hoc forensic attribution rather than prevention; suspicious arXiv ID (2605) suggests possibly unverified preprint.

title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Dario Pasquini; Martin Strohmeier; Carmela Troncoso
why_relevant: Introduces learned prompt-injection triggers designed to survive RAG preprocessing (chunking, filtering), demonstrating a novel indirect injection attack against RAG pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on attack methodology; does not propose defenses or calibration.

title: Neuro-RIT: Neuron-Guided Instruction Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
authors: Jaemin Kim; Jae O Lee; Sumyeong Ahn; Seo Yeon Park
why_relevant: Proposes a neuron-guided instruction tuning method to make RALMs robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved contexts, directly addressing the noisy retrieval and distraction robustness theme.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on a specific tuning technique rather than broad analysis or benchmark.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
authors: Hanyu Zhu; Lance Fiondella; Jiawei Yuan; Kai Zeng; Long Jiao
why_relevant: Proposes a neuron-guided genetic poisoning attack on RAG that explicitly targets knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence, relevant to adversarial corruption and conflict sections.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; assumes white-box neuron access which is a strong threat model.

title: Noise-Robust Abstractive Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Singon Kim
why_relevant: Proposes ACoRN, a noise-robust abstractive context compression method for RAG that targets irrelevant and misleading retrieved documents via data augmentation and fine-tuning.
why_not_or_caveat: Master's thesis; focused narrowly on compression rather than full RAG robustness pipeline.
suggested_section: Noisy retrieval / context filtering and compression

title: One Pic is All it Takes: Poisoning Visual Document Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Single Image
authors: Ezzeldin Shereen; Dan Ristea; Shae McFadden; Burak Hasircioglu; Vasilios Mavroudis; Chris Hicks
why_relevant: Demonstrates poisoning attacks against visual document RAG via a single adversarial image, addressing both retrieval and generation conditions in white- and black-box settings. Extends KB poisoning threat models to multimodal RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on visual modality; limited defense exploration.

title: One Shot Dominance: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Zhiyuan Chang; Mingyang Li; Xiaojun Jia; Junjie Wang; Yuekai Huang; Ziyou Jiang; Yang Liu; Qing Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a single-document knowledge poisoning attack (AuthChain) on RAG that overcomes LLMs' internal knowledge bias via authority signals, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and parametric-vs-retrieved conflict.

title: Open-RAG: Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Open-Source Large Language Models
authors: Shayekh Bin Islam; Md Asib Rahman; K S M Tozammel Hossain; Enamul Hoque; Shafiq Joty; Md Rizwan Parvez
why_relevant: Open-RAG explicitly trains models to contrast distractor passages that appear relevant but are misleading, and proposes a confidence-based hybrid adaptive retrieval mechanism deciding when to retrieve, directly addressing distraction and calibration/control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a method paper extending Self-RAG; robustness aspects are partial rather than the central contribution.
suggested_section: Calibration and adaptive retrieval / distraction-robust training

title: OpenDecoder: Open Large Language Model Decoding to Incorporate Document Quality in RAG
authors: Fengran Mo; Zhan Su; Yuchen Hui; Jinghan Zhang; Jia Ao Sun; Zheyuan Liu; Chao Zhang; Tetsuya Sakai; Jian-Yun Nie
why_relevant: Proposes a decoding method that integrates explicit document relevance/QPP signals to make RAG robust to noisy retrieved contexts, directly addressing noisy retrieval and control over evidence trust.

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Haozhen Wang; Haoyue Liu; Jionghao Zhu; Zhichao Wang; Yongxin Guo; Xiaoying Tang
why_relevant: Proposes a compound attack combining prompt injection and database poisoning against RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only paper without defenses; incremental over PoisonedRAG.

title: PRGB Benchmark: A Robust Placeholder-Assisted Algorithm for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhehao Tan; Yihan Jiao; Dan Yang; Lei Liu; Jie Feng; Duolin Sun; Yue Shen; Jian Wang; Peng Wei; Jinjie Gu
why_relevant: Introduces a fine-grained benchmark evaluating LLM robustness in RAG across multi-level noise filtering, combination, and reasoning, with a placeholder method to decouple parametric vs external knowledge—directly relevant to noisy retrieval and parametric-vs-context conflict evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on benchmarking rather than proposing defenses or calibration methods.

title: Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
authors: Gelei Deng; Yi Liu; Kailong Wang; Yuekang Li; Tianwei Zhang; Yang Liu
why_relevant: Introduces a RAG poisoning attack vector (Pandora) that injects malicious documents into the knowledge base to jailbreak GPTs, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary evaluation; focuses on jailbreaking rather than general RAG robustness.

title: Parallel Key-Value Cache Fusion for Position Invariant RAG
authors: Philhoon Oh; Jinwoo Shin; James Thorne
why_relevant: Proposes KV-Fusion to make RAG position-invariant, addressing lost-in-the-middle distraction and improving robustness to irrelevant passages.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on positional bias rather than broader robustness threats like adversarial or conflict cases.

title: Parenting: Optimizing Knowledge Selection of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Parameter Decoupling and Tailored Tuning
authors: Yongxin Xu; Ruizhe Zhang; Xinke Jiang; Yujie Feng; Yuzhen Xiao; Xinyu Ma; Runchuan Zhu; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a parameter-decoupling fine-tuning method to balance adherence to retrieved context vs robustness to noisy contexts, directly tackling knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval in RAG.

title: PassiveQA: A Three-Action Framework for Epistemically Calibrated Question Answering via Supervised Finetuning
authors: Madhav S Baidya
why_relevant: Proposes a three-action (Answer/Ask/Abstain) framework for RAG under incomplete information, directly addressing abstention, clarification, and epistemic calibration—core themes of the survey's calibration/control and OOD/uncertainty sections.
why_not_or_caveat: Single-author preprint with limited validation; focus is on training-time alignment rather than broader robustness.

title: Poisoned LangChain: Jailbreak LLMs by LangChain
authors: Ziqiu Wang; Jun Liu; Shengkai Zhang; Yang Yang
why_relevant: Proposes an indirect jailbreak attack via poisoning the external knowledge base used by LangChain RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: Post-training an LLM for RAG? Train on Self-Generated Demonstrations
authors: Matthew Finlayson; Ilia Kulikov; Daniel M. Bikel; Barlas Oguz; Xilun Chen; Aasish Pappu
why_relevant: Proposes self-generated demonstrations for RA-IT to teach LLMs to integrate retrievals properly and abstain on questions they likely answer wrong, directly addressing calibration/abstention and reducing hallucination under retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on training recipe rather than systematic robustness analysis; doesn't deeply study noisy/adversarial evidence.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (abstention and RAG training)

title: Principled Context Engineering for RAG: Statistical Guarantees via Conformal Prediction
authors: Debashish Chakraborty; Eugene Yang; Daniel Khashabi; Dawn Lawrie; Kevin Duh
why_relevant: Applies split conformal prediction to filter retrieved snippets with finite-sample coverage guarantees, directly addressing noisy retrieval and calibrated control over context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on pre-generation filtering rather than broader robustness issues like conflict or adversarial attacks.

title: PrismRAG: Boosting RAG Factuality with Distractor Resilience and Strategized Reasoning
authors: Mohammad Kachuee; Teja Gollapudi; Minseok Kim; Yin Huang; Kai Sun; Xiao Yang; Jiaqi Wang; Nirav Shah; Yue Liu; Aaron Colak; Anuj Kumar; Wen-tau Yih; Xin Luna Dong
why_relevant: PrismRAG fine-tunes LLMs for distractor resilience by training on QA pairs with synthetically generated semi-relevant distractors, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval robustness in RAG.

title: Prompt Perturbation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Language Models
authors: Zhibo Hu; Chen Wang; Yanfeng Shu; Helen; Paik; Liming Zhu
why_relevant: Proposes Gradient Guided Prompt Perturbation, an adversarial prefix attack targeting RAG retrieval to induce factually incorrect outputs, plus a neuron-activation-based detection defense. Directly addresses adversarial robustness of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompt-side perturbations rather than corpus poisoning; defense is detection-based.

title: QuCo-RAG: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Pre-training Corpus for Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Dehai Min; Kailin Zhang; Tongtong Wu; Lu Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes a dynamic RAG method that decides when to retrieve based on corpus-grounded uncertainty rather than poorly-calibrated model-internal signals, directly addressing calibration/control and long-tail knowledge gaps.

title: Quantifying Document Impact in RAG-LLMs
authors: Armin Gerami; Kazem Faghih; Ramani Duraiswami
why_relevant: Proposes Influence Score to quantify per-document impact in RAG, validated on PoisonedRAG attacks to detect malicious documents. Relevant to defense/attribution under adversarial corruption and explainability.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily an attribution metric; defense application is secondary.

title: Quantifying and Improving the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
authors: Shiping Yang; Jie Wu; Wenbiao Ding; Ning Wu; Shining Liang; Ming Gong; Hongzhi Li; Hengyuan Zhang; Angel X. Chang; Dongmei Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces SURE framework and SIG_Wiki benchmark to evaluate and improve RAG robustness against spurious (semantic-agnostic) features like formatting in retrieved documents, directly relevant to noisy retrieval and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on implicit/spurious feature noise rather than core adversarial or conflict scenarios.

title: Query-Level Uncertainty in Large Language Models
authors: Lihu Chen; Gerard de Melo; Fabian M. Suchanek; Gaël Varoquaux
why_relevant: Proposes query-level uncertainty estimation to decide when to invoke RAG, directly relevant to adaptive retrieval and calibration/control under unknown knowledge boundaries.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader uncertainty estimation; RAG invocation is one application.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: RADIANT: Retrieval AugmenteD entIty-context AligNmenT -- Introducing RAG-ability and Entity-Context Divergence
authors: Vipula Rawte; Rajarshi Roy; Gurpreet Singh; Danush Khanna; Yaswanth Narsupalli; Basab Ghosh; Abhay Gupta; Argha Kamal Samanta; Aditya Shingote; Aadi Krishna Vikram; Vinija Jain; Aman Chadha; Amit Sheth; Amitava Das
why_relevant: Introduces RAG-ability and Entity-Context Divergence metric to evaluate faithfulness of LLMs to retrieved evidence, and proposes a DPO-based alignment method to improve robustness under noisy contexts and knowledge conflicts.
why_not_or_caveat: Evaluation domain limited to news; metric novelty modest.

title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
authors: Tianjun Zhang; Shishir G. Patil; Naman Jain; Sheng Shen; Matei Zaharia; Ion Stoica; Joseph E. Gonzalez
why_relevant: RAFT fine-tunes LLMs with distractor documents to make them robust against irrelevant/noisy retrieved context, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on domain-specific adaptation rather than broad robustness taxonomy.

title: RAG Safety: Exploring Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tianzhe Zhao; Jiaoyan Chen; Yanchi Ru; Haiping Zhu; Nan Hu; Jun Liu; Qika Lin
why_relevant: First systematic study of data poisoning attacks on KG-based RAG, proposing a stealthy triple-insertion attack that creates misleading inference chains and analyzing robustness of LLMs to poisoned retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on KG-RAG rather than text-based RAG, so somewhat niche within adversarial RAG literature.

title: RAG-RL: Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via RL and Curriculum Learning
authors: Jerry Huang; Siddarth Madala; Risham Sidhu; Cheng Niu; Hao Peng; Julia Hockenmaier; Tong Zhang
why_relevant: RAG-RL trains the generator to identify and cite relevant passages among distractors, directly addressing robustness to imperfect retrieval and irrelevant contexts via RL and curriculum learning.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on improving generation under distractors rather than adversarial or conflict settings; evaluation limited to multi-hop QA.

title: RAG-RewardBench: Benchmarking Reward Models in Retrieval Augmented Generation for Preference Alignment
authors: Zhuoran Jin; Hongbang Yuan; Tianyi Men; Pengfei Cao; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark for reward models in RAG covering RAG-specific robustness scenarios including appropriate abstain and conflict robustness, directly relevant to calibration/control and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on reward model evaluation for preference alignment rather than robustness mechanisms themselves.

title: RAGRank: Using PageRank to Counter Poisoning in CTI LLM Pipelines
authors: Austin Jia; Avaneesh Ramesh; Zain Shamsi; Daniel Zhang; Alex Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a PageRank-based source credibility defense against RAG corpus poisoning attacks, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption category.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to CTI, but methodology generalizes.

title: RAGShaper: Eliciting Sophisticated Agentic RAG Skills via Automated Data Synthesis
authors: Zhengwei Tao; Bo Li; Jialong Wu; Guochen Yan; Huanyao Zhang; Jiahao Xu; Haitao Mi; Wentao Zhang
why_relevant: RAGShaper synthesizes agentic RAG training data with adversarial distractors (Perception/Cognition) and elicits error-correction trajectories, directly targeting robustness to noisy and distracting retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on training data synthesis rather than evaluation or calibration; robustness is a downstream claim.
suggested_section: Distraction and noisy retrieval: training-time defenses

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kiseung Kim; Jay-Yoon Lee
why_relevant: Proposes a relevance estimator that filters irrelevant retrieved contexts, enables abstention ('unanswerable'), and chooses between parametric and retrieved knowledge based on confidence—directly addressing noisy retrieval, calibration/control, and parametric-vs-retrieved conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA performance; robustness analysis is a secondary contribution rather than a comprehensive study.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Filtering Noisy Retrieval

title: REAR: A Relevance-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Junyi Li; Wayne Xin Zhao; Jing Liu; Ji-Rong Wen
why_relevant: REAR addresses noisy/irrelevant retrieval by adding a relevance assessment module and noise-resistant training, enabling the LLM to adaptively weigh external vs parametric knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA; does not address adversarial or OOD settings.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
authors: Fangyuan Xu; Weijia Shi; Eunsol Choi
why_relevant: RECOMP compresses retrieved documents and supports selective augmentation (returning empty when retrieval is irrelevant), directly addressing noisy/distracting retrieval and when-to-trust-retrieval control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary motivation is efficiency; robustness is a secondary benefit.

title: RIPRAG: Hack a Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Question-Answering System with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Meng Xi; Sihan Lv; Yechen Jin; Guanjie Cheng; Naibo Wang; Ying Li; Jianwei Yin
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box RL-based poisoning attack on RAG QA systems, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and benchmarking against defended RAG systems.

title: RPO: Retrieval Preference Optimization for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shi-Qi Yan; Quan Liu; Zhen-Hua Ling
why_relevant: Proposes a preference-optimization alignment method to handle knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge, adaptively trusting retrieval based on relevance, directly relevant to conflict resolution and control.

title: Rag and Roll: An End-to-End Evaluation of Indirect Prompt Manipulations in LLM-based Application Frameworks
authors: Gianluca De Stefano; Lea Schönherr; Giancarlo Pellegrino
why_relevant: End-to-end evaluation of indirect prompt injection attacks against RAG pipelines, examining how configuration choices affect attack success—directly relevant to adversarial corruption and robustness evaluation.

title: Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM Agents via Stealthy Style Transfer: Process-Level Attacks and Runtime Monitoring in RSV Space
authors: Xingfu Zhou; Pengfei Wang
why_relevant: Introduces a novel process-level poisoning attack on RAG agents via stylistic manipulation of retrieved documents, plus a runtime monitor defense, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence and process-level calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on reasoning style rather than factual content; somewhat narrow attack vector.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection

title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
authors: Mingrui Liu; Sixiao Zhang; Cheng Long; Kwok-Yan Lam
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in RAG contexts, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader prompt-injection defense with systems-level optimization; RAG is one of several evaluation settings.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
authors: Ziye Wang; Guanyu Wang; Kailong Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy word-level poisoning attack against RAG retrievers, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: Reinforced Internal-External Knowledge Synergistic Reasoning for Efficient Adaptive Search Agent
authors: Ziyang Huang; Xiaowei Yuan; Yiming Ju; Jun Zhao; Kang Liu
why_relevant: IKEA uses RL with a knowledge-boundary aware reward to decide when to retrieve vs rely on parametric knowledge, directly addressing adaptive retrieval control and avoiding noisy retrieval/knowledge conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is efficiency-oriented adaptive retrieval rather than explicit robustness evaluation under adversarial or noisy evidence.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Replace, Don't Expand: Mitigating Context Dilution in Multi-Hop RAG via Fixed-Budget Evidence Assembly
authors: Moshe Lahmy; Roi Yozevitch
why_relevant: Proposes a fixed-budget controller that actively replaces distractor passages with gap-closing evidence to mitigate context dilution in multi-hop RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-hop QA evidence assembly; does not address adversarial or conflict settings.

title: Resolving Conflicting Evidence in Automated Fact-Checking: A Study on Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
authors: Ziyu Ge; Yuhao Wu; Daniel Wai Kit Chin; Roy Ka-Wei Lee; Rui Cao
why_relevant: Introduces CONFACT, a dataset and evaluation of RAG models facing conflicting retrieved evidence from sources of varying credibility, directly studying retrieved-vs-retrieved conflict and proposing credibility-aware mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to fact-checking, but conflict-handling findings generalize.

title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conflict-Driven Summarization
authors: Juan Chen; Baolong Bi; Wei Zhang; Jingyan Sui; Xiaofei Zhu; Yuanzhuo Wang; Lingrui Mei; Shenghua Liu
why_relevant: Proposes CARE-RAG, a framework explicitly addressing knowledge conflicts between parametric and retrieved evidence and refining noisy retrieved content via conflict-driven summarization, directly relevant to conflict and noise robustness.

title: Rethinking LLM Parametric Knowledge as Post-retrieval Confidence for Dynamic Retrieval and Reranking
authors: Haoxiang Jin; Ronghan Li; Zixiang Lu; Qiguang Miao
why_relevant: Proposes confidence-based dynamic retrieval triggering and reranking using LLM hidden-state confidence to decide when to retrieve and which contexts to trust, directly addressing calibration/control and knowledge-boundary issues in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on a specific method rather than broad robustness analysis.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (when to retrieve / filter)

title: Rethinking the Reranker: Boundary-Aware Evidence Selection for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiashuo Sun; Pengcheng Jiang; Saizhuo Wang; Jiajun Fan; Heng Wang; Siru Ouyang; Ming Zhong; Yizhu Jiao; Chengsong Huang; Xueqiang Xu; Pengrui Han; Peiran Li; Jiaxin Huang; Ge Liu; Heng Ji; Jiawei Han
why_relevant: BAR-RAG addresses RAG brittleness under noisy retrieval by training a boundary-aware reranker/selector using generator uncertainty, directly targeting robustness and evidence filtering.

title: Retrieval Augmented Question Answering: When Should LLMs Admit Ignorance?
authors: Dingmin Wang; Ji Ma; Shankar Kumar
why_relevant: Proposes iterative chunked prompting to mitigate distractor noise in long-context RAG, and explicitly analyzes LLMs' failure to abstain when evidence is insufficient, directly relevant to calibration/abstention under unreliable retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Method is relatively simple; abstention analysis is observational rather than a new technique.
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention under Insufficient Evidence

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
authors: Chaitanya Sharma
metadata_topics: rag-core; noisy-retrieval; knowledge-conflict; adversarial-corruption; calibration-control; evaluation-benchmark
why_relevant: A comprehensive RAG survey explicitly covering robustness-oriented designs, noise/adversarial challenges, and evaluation benchmarks, overlapping significantly with this survey's scope.
why_not_or_caveat: As a broad survey, overlap is partial and it lacks focus depth on calibration/conflict; useful as a related-work reference.

title: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
authors: Lionel Wong; Ayman Ali; Raymond Xiong; Shannon Zeijang Shen; Yoon Kim; Monica Agrawal
why_relevant: Analyzes failure modes of RAG systems where retrieved content is technically accurate but pragmatically misleading, including decontextualization, omission of critical sources, and compliance with biased queries—relevant to reliability, context compliance, and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical) position paper; not a method or benchmark per se.
suggested_section: Reliability and pragmatic failure modes / domain risks

title: RetrievalQA: Assessing Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Short-form Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Zihan Zhang; Meng Fang; Ling Chen
why_relevant: Introduces RetrievalQA benchmark and TA-ARE method for adaptive retrieval, evaluating when LLMs should trigger retrieval—directly relevant to calibration/control over when to retrieve.
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve

title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG
authors: Boxi Yu; Yuzhong Zhang; Liting Lin; Lionel Briand; Emir Muñoz
why_relevant: Proposes a hallucination/faithfulness detector for RAG that flags unsupported or contradicted claims against retrieved context, and introduces an enhanced RAGTruth benchmark. Relevant to evaluation of context-faithfulness and detection of conflicts between generation and retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on post-hoc detection rather than mitigating noisy/adversarial retrieval directly.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
authors: Yulin Chen; Haoran Li; Yuan Sui; Yue Liu; Yufei He; Xiaoling Bai; Chi Fei; Yabo Li; Haozhe Ma; Yangqiu Song; Bryan Hooi
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks where malicious instructions are embedded in retrieved content, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompt injection broadly rather than RAG-specific poisoning pipelines.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection

title: RoseRAG: Robust Retrieval-augmented Generation with Small-scale LLMs via Margin-aware Preference Optimization
authors: Tianci Liu; Haoxiang Jiang; Tianze Wang; Ran Xu; Yue Yu; Linjun Zhang; Tuo Zhao; Haoyu Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a preference optimization method to make small LLMs robust to noisy retrieved documents in RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on SLMs and training strategy; limited scope beyond noise robustness.

title: SEReDeEP: Hallucination Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Models via Semantic Entropy and Context-Parameter Fusion
authors: Lei Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a hallucination detection method for RAG that combines semantic entropy probes with ReDeEP's decoupling of parametric vs contextual contributions, directly addressing knowledge conflict and uncertainty-based detection in RAG.
