why_not_or_caveat: Single-author arXiv preprint building incrementally on ReDeEP; limited novelty and validation.

title: SFR-RAG: Towards Contextually Faithful LLMs
authors: Xuan-Phi Nguyen; Shrey Pandit; Senthil Purushwalkam; Austin Xu; Hailin Chen; Yifei Ming; Zixuan Ke; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xong; Shafiq Joty
why_relevant: Introduces an instruction-tuned RAG LLM emphasizing contextual faithfulness, resilience to counterfactual/altered contexts, unanswerability handling, and distractor robustness, plus ContextualBench evaluation suite.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a model/benchmark release rather than focused robustness analysis.

title: SGIC: A Self-Guided Iterative Calibration Framework for RAG
authors: Guanhua Chen; Yutong Yao; Lidia S. Chao; Xuebo Liu; Derek F. Wong
why_relevant: Proposes a self-guided iterative calibration framework using uncertainty scores over documents and answers to refine RAG outputs, directly addressing calibration/control and uncertainty estimation under retrieval noise.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-hop QA accuracy rather than adversarial or conflict scenarios.

title: SciRerankBench: Benchmarking Rerankers Towards Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated LLMs
authors: Haotian Chen; Qingqing Long; Meng Xiao; Xiao Luo; Wei Ju; Chengrui Wang; Xuezhi Wang; Yuanchun Zhou; Hengshu Zhu
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark evaluating rerankers in RAG with noisy contexts, semantically similar but logically irrelevant contexts, and counterfactual contexts—directly relevant to noise, distraction, and conflict robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to scientific QA and focused on reranker evaluation rather than end-to-end RAG robustness methods.

title: Search Wisely: Mitigating Sub-optimal Agentic Searches By Reducing Uncertainty
authors: Peilin Wu; Mian Zhang; Xinlu Zhang; Xinya Du; Zhiyu Zoey Chen
why_relevant: Studies when an agentic RAG system should retrieve vs. rely on parametric knowledge, linking sub-optimal search to uncertainty about knowledge boundaries, and proposes an RL method (β-GRPO) using confidence thresholds to control retrieval decisions.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agentic search efficiency rather than handling noisy/adversarial evidence directly.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
authors: Sizhe Chen; Arman Zharmagambetov; Saeed Mahloujifar; Kamalika Chaudhuri; David Wagner; Chuan Guo
why_relevant: SecAlign defends LLMs against prompt injection from external data sources (including retrieved content) via preference optimization, directly relevant to adversarial corruption defenses in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on general LLM-integrated applications rather than RAG specifically, but threat model includes web retrieval.

title: Securing AI Agents Against Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Badrinath Ramakrishnan; Akshaya Balaji
why_relevant: Provides a benchmark and multi-layer defense framework for prompt injection attacks in RAG systems, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and evaluation aspects of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Unclear release/peer-review status; defense methods are fairly standard and benchmark details limited.

title: Selective Memory for Artificial Intelligence: Write-Time Gating with Hierarchical Archiving
authors: Oliver Zahn; Simran Chana
why_relevant: Proposes write-time salience gating for RAG to filter noisy/distractor content, compares to Self-RAG under distractor scaling, and evaluates robustness on adversarial benchmarks.
why_not_or_caveat: Non-peer-reviewed arXiv preprint with suspicious dating; claims (100% accuracy) should be treated cautiously.

title: Semantic Chameleon: Corpus-Dependent Poisoning Attacks and Defenses in RAG Systems
authors: Scott Thornton
why_relevant: Studies gradient-guided corpus poisoning attacks on RAG and evaluates hybrid retrieval as a defense, with multi-model and cross-corpus evaluation directly relevant to adversarial robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Independent preprint with suspicious arxiv id and forward-dated models (GPT-5.3); verify provenance before citing.

title: Semantic Grounding Index: Geometric Bounds on Context Engagement in RAG Systems
authors: Javier Marín
why_relevant: Proposes a geometric, calibration-friendly signal (SGI) for detecting ungrounded/hallucinated RAG responses, directly relevant to detection, abstention, and calibration under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Measures topical engagement rather than factual accuracy (negative result on TruthfulQA); limited to single-signal detection.

title: SilentRetrieval: Hijacking Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Semantically-Preserving Adversarial Data Poisoning
authors: Jiachen Qian
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy data poisoning attack on RAG corpora combining retrieval hijacking and generation manipulation, and evaluates defenses (reranking, hybrid retrieval, passage isolation), directly relevant to adversarial corruption.
why_not_or_caveat: Single-author arXiv preprint with a suspicious identifier (2605.xxxxx); provenance/quality should be verified.

title: Spa-VLM: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based VLM
authors: Lei Yu; Yechao Zhang; Ziqi Zhou; Yang Wu; Wei Wan; Minghui Li; Shengshan Hu; Pei Xiaobing; Jing Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy poisoning attack on RAG-based VLMs, extending RAG poisoning to multimodal knowledge bases and evaluating defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on VLM/multimodal setting rather than text-only RAG.

title: Studying Large Language Model Behaviors Under Context-Memory Conflicts With Real Documents
authors: Evgenii Kortukov; Alexander Rubinstein; Elisa Nguyen; Seong Joon Oh
why_relevant: Analyzes context-memory knowledge conflicts in RAG using real documents, identifying a parametric bias that hinders knowledge updating. Directly relevant to the survey's knowledge conflict section.

title: Supportiveness-based Knowledge Rewriting for Retrieval-augmented Language Modeling
authors: Zile Qiao; Wei Ye; Yong Jiang; Tong Mo; Pengjun Xie; Weiping Li; Fei Huang; Shikun Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge rewriter that filters noisy/misleading retrieved content using a supportiveness score, directly addressing robustness of RAG to unreliable retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on rewriting/compression rather than conflict, attacks, or calibration explicitly.

title: TRAQ: Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Question Answering via Conformal Prediction
authors: Shuo Li; Sangdon Park; Insup Lee; Osbert Bastani
why_relevant: TRAQ applies conformal prediction to RAG to provide statistical correctness guarantees over both retrieval and generation, addressing uncertainty quantification and calibration in RAG pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on coverage guarantees via prediction sets rather than noise/conflict/adversarial robustness directly.

title: The Confidence Dichotomy: Analyzing and Mitigating Miscalibration in Tool-Use Agents
authors: Weihao Xuan; Qingcheng Zeng; Heli Qi; Yunze Xiao; Junjue Wang; Naoto Yokoya
why_relevant: Studies how noisy evidence retrieval (web search) induces overconfidence in tool-use agents and proposes an RL framework to jointly optimize accuracy and calibration, directly relevant to calibration under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Framed as tool-use agents rather than RAG specifically, but evidence-tool analysis maps directly to retrieval noise.

title: The Cost of Context: Mitigating Textual Bias in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hoin Jung; Xiaoqian Wang
why_relevant: Identifies 'recorruption' in multimodal RAG where even oracle context degrades correct predictions due to attention collapse and positional bias, and proposes an inference-time mitigation (BAIR). Directly relevant to distraction and context-vs-internal-knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal (MLLM) setting rather than pure text RAG.

title: The Curse of Helpfulness: Inverse Scaling Law in Robustness to Distractor Instructions via DistractionIF
authors: Zeli Su; Zhankai Xu; Tianlei Chen; Longfei Zheng; Xiaolu Zhang; Jun Zhou; Wentao Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces DistractionIF benchmark measuring LLM robustness to instruction-like distractor noise in reference text for RAG/agent settings, revealing inverse scaling and proposing RL-based mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on benign instruction-like distractors rather than retrieval noise per se; overlaps with indirect prompt injection territory.

title: The Hidden Threat in Plain Text: Attacking RAG Data Loaders
authors: Alberto Castagnaro; Umberto Salviati; Mauro Conti; Luca Pajola; Simeone Pizzi
why_relevant: Introduces novel poisoning attacks targeting RAG data loaders via content obfuscation/injection in DOCX/HTML/PDF, with taxonomy and evaluation across loaders and end-to-end RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on ingestion-stage attacks rather than defenses or calibration.

title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Copying Is Easier to Induce Than Recall
authors: Mehrdad Farahani; Franziska Penzkofer; Richard Johansson
why_relevant: Mechanistic study of how LLMs arbitrate between parametric knowledge and (false) retrieved context, with a steering intervention to shift copy-vs-recall behavior. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and context compliance in RAG settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is mechanistic/interventional rather than proposing a deployable RAG robustness method.

title: Topic-FlipRAG: Topic-Orientated Adversarial Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
authors: Yuyang Gong; Zhuo Chen; Jiawei Liu; Miaokun Chen; Fengchang Yu; Wei Lu; Xiaofeng Wang; Xiaozhong Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a topic-level opinion manipulation poisoning attack against RAG and evaluates existing defenses (perplexity, reranking, paraphrasing), directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defense robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on opinion manipulation rather than general robustness.

title: Towards Action Hijacking of Large Language Model-based Agent
authors: Yuyang Zhang; Kangjie Chen; Jiaxin Gao; Ronghao Cui; Run Wang; Lina Wang; Tianwei Zhang
why_relevant: Presents a novel attack on LLM-agent RAG pipelines that exploits the retrieval mechanism to extract and assemble harmful knowledge, bypassing safety filters. Relevant to adversarial corruption / indirect prompt injection on RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent action hijacking rather than QA-style RAG robustness; not centered on defense/calibration.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and prompt injection attacks on RAG

title: Towards Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation Based on Knowledge Graph: A Comparative Analysis
authors: Hazem Amamou; Stéphane Gagnon; Alan Davoust; Anderson R. Avila
why_relevant: Evaluates RAG robustness across noise, integration, negative rejection, and counterfactual scenarios using RGB, comparing GraphRAG variants as a defense strategy.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited novelty; mainly a comparative analysis with prompt/KG customizations on an existing benchmark.

title: Towards Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Review of Threats, Defenses and Benchmarks
authors: Yanming Mu; Hao Hu; Feiyang Li; Qiao Yuan; Jiang Wu; Zichuan Liu; Pengcheng Liu; Mei Wang; Hongwei Zhou; Yuling Liu
why_relevant: End-to-end survey of RAG security threats (poisoning, adversarial, membership inference), defenses, and benchmarks, directly overlapping with the adversarial corruption and evaluation sections of the target survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on security/privacy rather than broader robustness aspects like distraction, calibration, or knowledge conflict.

title: Towards Unsupervised Adversarial Document Detection in Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Patrick Levi
why_relevant: Proposes an unsupervised detector for adversarial/poisoned context documents in RAG using activations, embeddings, and entropy-based uncertainty, directly addressing defense against retrieval poisoning.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary study with limited scale (100 HotpotQA questions, simple Grubb's test).

title: Transparentize the Internal and External Knowledge Utilization in LLMs with Trustworthy Citation
authors: Jiajun Shen; Tong Zhou; Yubo Chen; Delai Qiu; Shengping Liu; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Addresses when to trust parametric vs retrieved knowledge in RAG, with confidence calibration (ECE) and trustworthy citation generation, directly relevant to knowledge conflict and calibration/control under unreliable retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on citation/attribution rather than core robustness attacks; relevance is via calibration and internal-vs-external knowledge use.

title: Tricking Retrievers with Influential Tokens: An Efficient Black-Box Corpus Poisoning Attack
authors: Cheng Wang; Yiwei Wang; Yujun Cai; Bryan Hooi
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box corpus poisoning attack (DIGA) targeting dense retrievers in RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only paper without defense or calibration contributions.

title: Trusted Uncertainty in Large Language Models: A Unified Framework for Confidence Calibration and Risk-Controlled Refusal
authors: Markus Oehri; Giulia Conti; Kaviraj Pather; Alexandre Rossi; Laia Serra; Adrian Parody; Rogvi Johannesen; Aviaja Petersen; Arben Krasniqi
why_relevant: Proposes a unified calibration and risk-controlled refusal framework that fuses retrieval compatibility and verifier signals into calibrated confidence with conformal guarantees, directly relevant to calibration, abstention, and uncertainty-driven control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Not RAG-specific; suspicious author affiliations and placeholder emails suggest possible low-quality/AI-generated paper—verify before citing.

title: TruthRL: Incentivizing Truthful LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zhepei Wei; Xiao Yang; Kai Sun; Jiaqi Wang; Rulin Shao; Sean Chen; Mohammad Kachuee; Teja Gollapudi; Tony Liao; Nicolas Scheffer; Rakesh Wanga; Anuj Kumar; Yu Meng; Wen-tau Yih; Xin Luna Dong
why_relevant: TruthRL uses RL with a ternary reward to teach LLMs to abstain when uncertain, directly addressing calibration/abstention and knowledge boundary recognition in both retrieval and non-retrieval setups, including noisy RAG contexts.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader than RAG; robustness to noisy retrieval is a secondary evaluation.

title: TruthfulRAG: Resolving Factual-level Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs
authors: Shuyi Liu; Yuming Shang; Xi Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes a KG-based method to resolve factual conflicts between parametric and retrieved knowledge in RAG, directly addressing the knowledge conflict axis of the survey.

title: U-NIAH: Unified RAG and LLM Evaluation for Long Context Needle-In-A-Haystack
authors: Yunfan Gao; Yun Xiong; Wenlong Wu; Zijing Huang; Bohan Li; Haofen Wang
why_relevant: Introduces a unified NIAH-based benchmark evaluating RAG vs long-context LLMs under retrieval noise, chunk ordering, and distractors, identifying error patterns like omission, hallucination, and self-doubt relevant to robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on long-context NIAH evaluation rather than proposing robustness methods.

title: Unanswerability Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Xiangyu Peng; Prafulla Kumar Choubey; Caiming Xiong; Chien-Sheng Wu
why_relevant: Introduces UAEval4RAG, a benchmark for evaluating RAG systems' ability to reject six categories of unanswerable queries (underspecified, false-presupposition, nonsensical, modality-limited, safety, OOD), directly relevant to abstention, OOD, and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
suggested_section: Evaluation benchmarks for abstention and unanswerability

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Simon Binz; Heydar Soudani; Faegheh Hasibi
why_relevant: Proposes a learnable uncertainty quantification method for multimodal RAG that captures uncertainty from retrieval and modality inputs, directly relevant to calibration and reliability under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal VQA setting; not addressing adversarial or conflict aspects.

title: Understanding Parametric Knowledge Injection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Minghao Tang; Shiyu Ni; Jingtong Wu; Zengxin Han; Keping Bi
why_relevant: Systematically analyzes parametric RAG vs token-based RAG under knowledge conflicts and retrieval noise, providing evidence on robustness and faithfulness with a new benchmark.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is understanding parametric injection mechanism; robustness is one of several axes.

title: Unraveling and Mitigating Retriever Inconsistencies in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Mingda Li; Xinyu Li; Yifan Chen; Wenfeng Xuan; Weinan Zhang
why_relevant: Analyzes retriever inconsistency and decomposes RALM degeneration into retriever error, extraction error, hallucination, and lucky guess, then proposes an ensemble-of-retrievers method to adaptively select knowledge sources and reduce reader errors.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on ODQA inconsistency rather than adversarial or conflict settings; relevance is primarily to noisy retrieval and adaptive retrieval control.
suggested_section: Noisy Retrieval and Adaptive Retrieval Control

title: When Iterative RAG Beats Ideal Evidence: A Diagnostic Study in Scientific Multi-hop Question Answering
authors: Mahdi Astaraki; Mohammad Arshi Saloot; Ali Shiraee Kasmaee; Hamidreza Mahyar; Soheila Samiee
why_relevant: Diagnostic study of iterative vs static RAG identifying failure modes including distractor latches, coverage gaps, composition failures, and stopping miscalibration in scientific multi-hop QA.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (chemistry) and focused on iterative RAG efficacy rather than adversarial robustness or conflict.

title: When to Trust: A Causality-Aware Calibration Framework for Accurate Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jing Ren; Bowen Li; Ziqi Xu; Xikun Zhang; Haytham Fayek; Xiaodong Li
why_relevant: Proposes a calibration framework for KG-RAG addressing overconfidence under unreliable/incomplete retrieved subgraphs, using counterfactual prompting and re-scoring to better align confidence with correctness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on KG-RAG specifically rather than general text RAG.

title: Who Taught the Lie? Responsibility Attribution for Poisoned Knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang; Haoran Xin; Yuxi Chen; Zhuqing Liu; Biao Yi; Tong Li; Lihai Nie; Zheli Liu; Minghong Fang
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box responsibility attribution framework to identify poisoned texts in RAG knowledge bases, directly addressing adversarial corruption and forensics under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on post-hoc attribution rather than prevention or calibration; narrower than general robustness.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
authors: Quang Hieu Pham; Hoang Ngo; Anh Tuan Luu; Dat Quoc Nguyen
why_relevant: Introduces WhoQA, a benchmark for evaluating LLM behavior under retrieved-vs-retrieved knowledge conflicts arising from same-name entities, directly relevant to the conflict and evaluation sections.

title: Whose Facts Win? LLM Source Preferences under Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Jakob Schuster; Vagrant Gautam; Katja Markert
why_relevant: Studies inter-context knowledge conflicts in RAG, examining how LLMs resolve conflicting evidence based on source credibility and revealing repetition-based vulnerabilities akin to disinformation attacks. Proposes a fine-tuning mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on source credibility dimension rather than the full breadth of RAG robustness.

title: Windsock is Dancing: Adaptive Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shu Zhao; Tianyi Shen; Nilesh Ahuja; Omesh Tickoo; Vijaykrishnan Narayanan
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive decision module for when/what to retrieve and noise-resistant instruction tuning for MRAG, addressing retrieval necessity and robustness to irrelevant retrieved documents.
why_not_or_caveat: Multimodal focus; not centrally about adversarial or conflict settings.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.804/)] Your RAG is Unfair: Exposing Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoor Attacks
why_relevant: Introduces BiasRAG, a backdoor attack on RAG via compromised query encoders and poisoned documents targeting fairness, expanding the threat landscape of adversarial corruption in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on fairness-specific backdoors rather than general robustness or defenses.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.717/)] The Silent Saboteur: Imperceptible Adversarial Attacks against Black-Box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
why_relevant: Proposes an imperceptible black-box adversarial attack against RAG that perturbs a target document to enter top-k retrieval and steer LLM answers, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and retrieval attacks.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Retrieval and Poisoning Attacks

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1291/)] The RAG Paradox: A Black-Box Attack Exploiting Unintentional Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
why_relevant: Proposes a realistic black-box corpus poisoning attack on RAG systems that exploits source disclosure, producing natural-looking poisoned documents that degrade RAG performance.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses solely on attack methodology; no defense or calibration component.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13757)] Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box adversarial ranking poisoning attack on RAG targeting opinion manipulation in open-ended controversial topics, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on opinion-polarity manipulation rather than factual QA poisoning.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06628)] Does Vec2Text Pose a New Corpus Poisoning Threat?
why_relevant: Proposes a novel corpus poisoning attack against dense retrievers using Vec2Text embedding inversion, which doesn't require model weights and can scale, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on dense retriever poisoning rather than end-to-end RAG generation, but retrieval poisoning is a key threat vector.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01705)] Data Extraction Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoors
why_relevant: Proposes a backdoor-based data extraction attack on RAG systems, exposing privacy vulnerabilities in retrieval databases through poisoned fine-tuning.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy extraction rather than answer-correctness robustness, but fits adversarial corruption scope.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17832)] MM-PoisonRAG: Disrupting Multimodal RAG with Local and Global Poisoning Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes localized and globalized knowledge poisoning attacks against multimodal RAG, evaluates across retrievers/MLLMs, and tests defenses—directly relevant to adversarial corruption in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG poisoning specifically; less central to text-only RAG robustness.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21315)] Tricking Retrievers with Influential Tokens: An Efficient Black-Box Corpus Poisoning Attack
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box corpus poisoning attack (DIGA) against RAG retrievers, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21680)] Hoist with His Own Petard: Inducing Guardrails to Facilitate Denial-of-Service Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLMs
why_relevant: Proposes MutedRAG, a denial-of-service poisoning attack that injects jailbreak prompts into the knowledge base to trigger LLM guardrails, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Injection Attacks

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06579)] POISONCRAFT: Practical Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
why_relevant: POISONCRAFT is a practical, query-agnostic poisoning attack on RAG that injects adversarial documents to manipulate retrieval and generation, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11548)] One shot dominance: Knowledge poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented generation systems
why_relevant: Proposes AuthChain, a single-document knowledge poisoning attack on RAG that exploits retrieval ranking and overcomes LLM internal-knowledge bias via authority signals, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and knowledge conflict.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23828)] Spa-VLM: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based VLM
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy poisoning attack on multi-modal RAG-based VLMs, injecting adversarial image-text pairs into the knowledge base to mislead generation, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on VLM/multimodal setting rather than text-only RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11415)] Bias Amplification in RAG: Poisoning Knowledge Retrieval to Steer LLMs
why_relevant: Proposes a poisoning attack on RAG that manipulates retrieval to amplify model biases, plus a dual-stage defense, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus on fairness/bias amplification rather than factual correctness, a narrower angle than typical RAG poisoning.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08862)] RAG Safety: Exploring Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: First systematic study of data poisoning attacks against KG-based RAG, injecting perturbation triples to mislead multi-hop reasoning; analyzes retrieval vs generation stage vulnerabilities and LLM robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses specifically on KG-RAG rather than text-based RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03110)] Token-Level Precise Attack on RAG: Searching for the Best Alternatives to Mislead Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a token-level attack on RAG that jointly targets retrieval and generation, injecting malicious passages into the knowledge base to mislead the reader. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption / Poisoning Attacks on RAG

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04276)] A Few Words Can Distort Graphs: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes knowledge poisoning attacks on GraphRAG via minimal text edits, showing defenses fail; directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG knowledge bases.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on GraphRAG variant rather than standard RAG.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10008)] RIPRAG: Hack a Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Question-Answering System with Reinforcement Learning
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box RL-based poisoning attack against RAG systems, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption axis of the survey.

title: [[<ins>arxiv</ins>](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15435)] HV-Attack: Hierarchical Visual Attack for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a visual adversarial attack on multimodal RAG that disrupts both retriever and generator via imperceptible image perturbations, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG attacks; no defense or calibration aspect.

title: \[[ACL Findings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19134)\]\[[Github](https://github.com/ZhishanQ/QuCo-RAG)\] QuCo-RAG: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Pre-training Corpus for Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a dynamic RAG triggering mechanism based on pre-training corpus statistics to decide when to retrieve, addressing miscalibration of internal confidence signals and long-tail knowledge gaps.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retrieval triggering rather than handling noisy/adversarial evidence directly.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: \[[ICML](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03181)\] C-RAG: Certified Generation Risks for Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
why_relevant: C-RAG provides conformal risk control for RAG generation, certifying upper bounds on generation risks including under test-time distribution shifts, directly relevant to calibration and uncertainty in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on certified risk guarantees rather than specific noise/conflict/adversarial scenarios.

title: \[[WWW](https://openreview.net/forum?id=bwnWs4us0x#discussion)\] Traceback of Poisoned Texts in Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes RAGForensics, a post-hoc traceback system to identify poisoned texts in RAG knowledge databases, directly addressing adversarial corruption defense.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on forensic traceback rather than inference-time robustness; complementary to mainstream defenses.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00935)\] Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes an evaluation framework and instruction-based methods for LLMs to detect, localize, and respond to parametric-vs-contextual knowledge conflicts, directly relevant to the conflict and calibration sections.
why_not_or_caveat: Uses synthetic conflicts rather than real retrieval pipelines.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08416)\] Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
why_relevant: PANDORA introduces a RAG poisoning attack vector that uses maliciously crafted documents to indirectly jailbreak GPTs, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval sources.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary evaluation only; focused on jailbreak rather than general RAG robustness.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04287)\] CONFLARE: CONFormal LArge language model REtrieval
why_relevant: Applies conformal prediction to RAG retrieval to quantify uncertainty and set similarity thresholds with statistical coverage guarantees, directly relevant to calibration/control and uncertainty quantification in retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retrieval-side calibration only, with a small medical QA demonstration.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07437)\] Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
why_relevant: Surveys RAG evaluation frameworks, metrics, and benchmarks including aspects of retrieval quality, faithfulness, and robustness-relevant evaluation dimensions.
why_not_or_caveat: General evaluation survey, not specifically focused on robustness/unreliable evidence.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00944)\] Unveil the Duality of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Theoretical Analysis and Practical Solution
why_relevant: Provides a token-level theoretical framework for trading off benefit vs detriment of retrieved evidence (including noisy/conflicting passages) and a method (Tok-RAG) for collaborative pure-LLM/RAG decoding to avoid being misled.
suggested_section: Calibration and control / parametric vs retrieved knowledge

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05794)\] RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a relevance estimator that filters irrelevant retrieved contexts, provides confidence-based decoding strategies including abstention ('unanswerable') and falling back to parametric knowledge, directly addressing distraction by noisy retrieval and calibration/control.
suggested_section: Calibration and control / filtering noisy retrieval

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18948)\] RevPRAG: Revealing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through LLM Activation Analysis
why_relevant: RevPRAG detects RAG poisoning attacks via LLM activation analysis, directly addressing adversarial corruption defenses in RAG.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02968)\] FlipedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box poisoning/opinion-manipulation attack against RAG retrievers, demonstrating corpus poisoning vulnerabilities and evaluating defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on opinion manipulation rather than general factual robustness; defenses analysis is limited.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Retrieval Attacks

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05587)\] Quantifying the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
why_relevant: Proposes SURE, a framework and benchmark for quantifying RAG robustness to spurious (semantic-agnostic) features in retrieved documents, with training-based mitigation strategies.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on implicit/spurious features (format, style) rather than core noise/conflict/adversarial issues.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21157)\] Real-Time Evaluation Models for RAG: Who Detects Hallucinations Best?
why_relevant: Benchmarks reference-free real-time hallucination/confidence evaluation models for RAG (LLM-as-Judge, HHEM, Prometheus, Lynx, TLM), directly relevant to calibration, trust scoring, and abstention in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Short technical report rather than rigorous research paper; limited novelty.
suggested_section: Calibration and hallucination detection for RAG

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04062)\] QE-RAG: A Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark for Query Entry Errors
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark evaluating RAG robustness to noisy/corrupted user queries (typos, keyboard/visual errors) and proposes a robust retriever and query correction method, directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable inputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on query-side noise rather than retrieved-evidence noise, which is a slightly different angle than most survey categories.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18041)\] RAG LLMs are Not Safer: A Safety Analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
why_relevant: Analyzes how RAG changes LLM safety profiles, showing safe models with safe documents can produce unsafe outputs, and evaluates red-teaming methods in RAG settings. Relevant to robustness/safety of RAG under realistic evidence conditions.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on safety/jailbreak rather than factual robustness, noise, or conflict per se.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and safety of RAG

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06956)\] Investigating the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation at the Query Level
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates RAG pipeline robustness under query-level perturbations (typos, redundancy, formality, ambiguity) across retrievers and LLMs, contributing an evaluation framework relevant to robustness/benchmarking.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on query perturbations rather than evidence corruption or conflict; tangential to adversarial/conflict aspects.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20324)\] RAG Security and Privacy: Formalizing the Threat Model and Attack Surface
why_relevant: Proposes a formal threat model and taxonomy for RAG attacks including poisoning and membership inference, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on security/privacy formalization rather than defenses or robustness mechanisms; limited coverage of other survey dimensions.

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09319)\] Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Provides a unified benchmark of knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption and evaluation aspects of robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on privacy/extraction attacks rather than poisoning or prompt injection, a narrower slice of adversarial robustness.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.18122v1)\] Poisoned LangChain: Jailbreak LLMs by LangChain
why_relevant: Proposes Poisoned-LangChain, an indirect jailbreak attack via poisoned RAG knowledge bases, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on Chinese LLMs and jailbreak scenario; limited defense analysis.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption / Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection

title: \[[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.04642)\] TRAQ: Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Question Answering via Conformal Prediction
why_relevant: TRAQ applies conformal prediction to RAG to provide statistical coverage guarantees on answer correctness, addressing uncertainty in both retrieval and generation stages.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on coverage guarantees rather than robustness to noise/attacks directly.

title: A MapReduce Approach to Effectively Utilize Long Context Information in Retrieval Augmented Language Models
authors: Gongbo Zhang; Zihan Xu; Qiao Jin; Fangyi Chen; Yilu Fang; Yi Liu; Justin F. Rousseau; Ziyang Xu; Zhiyong Lu; Chunhua Weng; Yifan Peng
why_relevant: Proposes a map-reduce RAG framework to mitigate lost-in-the-middle and irrelevant context distraction, with analysis of conflicting context resolution and a preflight check to decide when extra processing is needed.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on medical QA application; not a central robustness study.

title: A Troublemaker with Contagious Jailbreak Makes Chaos in Honest Towns
authors: Tianyi Men; Pengfei Cao; Zhuoran Jin; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Proposes a retrieval-suffix-based poisoning/jailbreak attack on agent memory (RAG) that propagates across multi-agent systems, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is multi-agent contagion rather than standard RAG robustness; tangential to core single-system RAG attacks.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Propagation in Agentic RAG

title: ADAM: A Systematic Data Extraction Attack on Agent Memory via Adaptive Querying
authors: Xingyu Lyu; Jianfeng He; Ning Wang; Yidan Hu; Tao Li; Danjue Chen; Shixiong Li; Yimin Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a privacy/data-extraction attack against RAG-style memory in LLM agents, relevant to adversarial robustness of retrieval-augmented systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy leakage from agent memory rather than evidence reliability or generation robustness; tangential to core RAG robustness themes.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG

title: Adaptive Retrieval helps Reasoning in LLMs -- but mostly if it's not used
authors: Srijan Shakya; Anamaria-Roberta Hartl; Sepp Hochreiter; Korbinian Pöppel
why_relevant: Studies adaptive retrieval as a metacognitive decision of when to retrieve, showing static retrieval injects noise while the model's choice to forgo retrieval correlates with confidence/correctness. Directly relevant to calibration/control (when to retrieve) and uncertainty-aware RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Small-scale empirical study on math benchmarks with a single 8B model; limited methodological novelty.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Adversarial Yet Cooperative: Multi-Perspective Reasoning in Retrieved-Augmented Language Models
authors: Can Xu; Lingyong Yan; Jiayi Wu; Haosen Wang; Shuaiqiang Wang; Yuchen Li; Jizhou Huang; Dawei Yin; Xiang Li
why_relevant: Proposes a reasoner-verifier multi-agent RAG framework with uncertainty/entropy-based process rewards to handle partial, conflicting, or misleading retrieved documents, relevant to calibration/control and conflict handling.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is RL reward design for agentic RAG rather than systematic robustness study; robustness to unreliable evidence is motivational rather than the main contribution.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
authors: Hanrong Zhang; Jingyuan Huang; Kai Mei; Yifei Yao; Zhenting Wang; Chenlu Zhan; Hongwei Wang; Yongfeng Zhang
why_relevant: ASB benchmarks attacks (including memory/RAG poisoning, indirect prompt injection, backdoors) and defenses on LLM agents, covering retrieval-stage adversarial corruption relevant to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Scope is broader LLM-agent security, not purely RAG; only memory poisoning and IPI directly intersect with the survey.

title: Asking For An Old Friend: Diagnosing and Mitigating Temporal Failure Modes in LLM-based Statutory Question Answering
authors: Max Prior; Andreas Schultz; Matthias Grabmair
why_relevant: Studies temporal knowledge conflict between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence in legal QA, including recency bias and RAG-based mitigation with temporal filtering. Provides a benchmark for diagnosing failure modes relevant to context compliance and conflict resolution.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (German statutory law) and narrowly focused on temporal validity rather than broad RAG robustness.

title: Benchmarking Deep Search over Heterogeneous Enterprise Data
authors: Prafulla Kumar Choubey; Xiangyu Peng; Shilpa Bhagavath; Kung-Hsiang Huang; Caiming Xiong; Chien-Sheng Wu
why_relevant: HERB benchmark evaluates RAG over heterogeneous enterprise data with realistic noise and includes unanswerable queries, supporting evaluation of retrieval failure modes and abstention under unsupported claims.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a deep-search multi-hop benchmark; robustness/unanswerability is secondary rather than central.

title: Beyond Component Strength: Synergistic Integration and Adaptive Calibration in Multi-Agent RAG Systems
authors: Jithin Krishnan
why_relevant: Studies multi-agent RAG reliability via ablations on adversarial and edge-case queries, focusing on abstention, ensemble verification, adaptive confidence thresholding, and inconsistent labeling artifacts—directly touching calibration/control and evaluation under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Very small-scale study (50 queries, single setup) and limited methodological novelty; findings are preliminary.

title: Bilevel Optimization for Covert Memory Tampering in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Architectures (XAMT)
authors: Akhil Sharma; Shaikh Yaser Arafat; Jai Kumar Sharma; Ken Huang
why_relevant: Proposes a bilevel optimization framework for covert poisoning of RAG knowledge bases (XAMT-RAG), evaluated on SafeRAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval memory.
why_not_or_caveat: Half the paper focuses on MARL replay buffers, not RAG; experimental section is largely protocol rather than results.

title: BlendFilter: Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Query Generation Blending and Knowledge Filtering
authors: Haoyu Wang; Ruirui Li; Haoming Jiang; Jinjin Tian; Zhengyang Wang; Chen Luo; Xianfeng Tang; Monica Cheng; Tuo Zhao; Jing Gao
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge filtering module to remove irrelevant retrieved passages and blends query augmentations to reduce noisy retrieval impact, relevant to the noisy retrieval and filtering subsection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on QA performance improvement rather than systematic robustness analysis.

title: Chain-based Adaptive Reconfiguration Over Lattices for Hallucination Reduction
authors: Joan Vendrell Gallart; Solmaz Kia; Russell Bent; Michael Grosskopf
why_relevant: Proposes a test-time hallucination detection and mitigation framework grounded in trusted context, compared to RAG baselines, addressing semantic uncertainty and reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Not directly focused on RAG robustness under noisy/adversarial retrieval; uses trusted axioms rather than retrieved evidence.

title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
authors: Hailey Onweller; Elias Lumer; Austin Huber; Pia Ramchandani; Vamse Kumar Subbiah; Corey Feld
why_relevant: Introduces an evaluation framework for citation reliability in deep research RAG agents, measuring link validity, relevance, and factual accuracy, and shows factual accuracy degrades as retrieval depth scales—relevant to evaluation of unreliable evidence and citation trustworthiness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on citation/attribution evaluation rather than robustness mechanisms; tangential to noise/conflict/adversarial axes.

title: Claim-Selective Certification for High-Risk Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shao Kan
why_relevant: Proposes a claim-level certification and abstain/partial/conflict action policy for medical RAG under mixed evidence, addressing knowledge conflict, selective abstention, and calibration of action decisions with dedicated metrics (UCCR, PAU).
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical) and uses weak-label protocol with limited generality; relies on template decomposition and cue-based scoring.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Conflict Handling

title: CoCoA: Collaborative Chain-of-Agents for Parametric-Retrieved Knowledge Synergy
authors: Yi Jiang; Sendong Zhao; Jianbo Li; Haochun Wang; Lizhe Zhang; Yan Liu; Bing Qin
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-agent framework that explicitly synergizes parametric and retrieved knowledge, addressing the parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflict and mitigating cases where retrieved content misleads generation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on performance improvement rather than systematic robustness analysis; conflict handling is implicit.

title: Compressing Long Context for Enhancing RAG with AMR-based Concept Distillation
authors: Kaize Shi; Xueyao Sun; Qing Li; Guandong Xu
why_relevant: Proposes AMR-based concept distillation to compress retrieved documents and filter noisy/irrelevant content, addressing distraction from noisy retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on context compression rather than explicit robustness evaluation under adversarial or conflicting evidence.

title: Context Quality Matters in Training Fusion-in-Decoder for Extractive Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Kosuke Akimoto; Kunihiro Takeoka; Masafumi Oyamada
why_relevant: Analyzes how context quality (proportion of relevant vs irrelevant passages) during FiD training affects robustness at inference, and proposes a cross-attention bias method to mitigate overfitting to specific context quality.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on FiD-specific training dynamics rather than general LLM RAG robustness.
suggested_section: Noisy retrieval and training under irrelevant passages

title: Context Shapes LLMs Retrieval-Augmented Fact-Checking Effectiveness
authors: Pietro Bernardelle; Stefano Civelli; Kevin Roitero; Gianluca Demartini
why_relevant: Analyzes how context length and evidence position affect LLM fact-checking accuracy, demonstrating lost-in-the-middle degradation and parametric vs evidence trade-offs relevant to distraction and knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on fact-checking rather than general RAG; limited to positional/length analysis.

title: Context-Length Robustness in Question Answering Models: A Comparative Empirical Study
authors: Trishita Dhara; Siddhesh Sheth
why_relevant: Empirically studies how injecting irrelevant context degrades QA accuracy while preserving the answer-bearing evidence, directly relevant to distraction and context dilution in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited novelty; small-scale empirical study on SQuAD/HotpotQA, not specifically about retrieval pipelines.

title: DRAINCODE: Stealthy Energy Consumption Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Context Poisoning
authors: Yanlin Wang; Jiadong Wu; Tianyue Jiang; Mingwei Liu; Jiachi Chen; Chong Wang; Ensheng Shi; Xilin Liu; Yuchi Ma; Zibin Zheng
why_relevant: Introduces a novel RAG context-poisoning attack targeting computational efficiency (energy/latency) in code generation, expanding the threat model for adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation and focuses on resource exhaustion rather than content correctness; tangential to mainstream RAG robustness concerns.

title: Defenses Against Prompt Attacks Learn Surface Heuristics
authors: Shawn Li; Chenxiao Yu; Zhiyu Ni; Hao Li; Charith Peris; Chaowei Xiao; Yue Zhao
why_relevant: Analyzes failure modes of supervised fine-tuning defenses against prompt injection, including indirect injection via retrieved content relevant to RAG. Identifies shortcut biases (position, token trigger, topic) that cause over-rejection, informing defense design for RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on prompt-injection defenses generally rather than RAG-specific pipelines; RAG is one motivating application.

title: Detecting AI Hallucinations in Finance: An Information-Theoretic Method Cuts Hallucination Rate by 92%
authors: Mainak Singha
why_relevant: Proposes a hallucination detection method for RAG that combines semantic entropy with an evidence-capacity measure via perplexity decomposition, targeting cases where models ignore or conflict with retrieved evidence. Relevant to calibration/abstention and detecting unsupported answers.
why_not_or_caveat: Small (n=200) synthetic financial QA evaluation; limited validation and narrow domain.

title: ECoRAG: Evidentiality-guided Compression for Long Context RAG
authors: Yeonseok Jeong; Jinsu Kim; Dohyeon Lee; Seung-won Hwang
why_relevant: ECoRAG compresses retrieved documents based on evidentiality, explicitly filtering distractors and irrelevant content, and adaptively decides when more retrieval is needed—relevant to noisy retrieval, distraction, and retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary framing is efficiency/compression for ODQA rather than robustness per se.
suggested_section: Distraction and Noisy Retrieval / Filtering and Compression

title: Efficient Context Selection for Long-Context QA: No Tuning, No Iteration, Just Adaptive-$k$
authors: Chihiro Taguchi; Seiji Maekawa; Nikita Bhutani
why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive method to dynamically decide how many passages to retrieve based on similarity score distributions, addressing the control problem of when/how much to retrieve and reducing noisy/irrelevant context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency and accuracy rather than robustness per se; touches calibration-of-retrieval-size only indirectly.

title: Efficient Test-Time Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Hailong Yin; Bin Zhu; Jingjing Chen; Chong-Wah Ngo
why_relevant: Proposes a test-time RAG framework that addresses irrelevant/noisy retrieved documents via stable organized retrieval combinations and consensus-based majority voting over candidate responses, directly targeting noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is largely on efficiency; robustness to noise is a secondary motivation rather than systematic study of adversaries or conflicts.

title: Enhancing Legal LLMs through Metadata-Enriched RAG Pipelines and Direct Preference Optimization
authors: Suyash Maniyar; Deepali Singh; Rohith Reddy
why_relevant: Proposes DPO training to enforce safe refusal when retrieved context is insufficient, and improves retrieval to reduce errors in legal RAG—directly addressing abstention/control and noisy retrieval failure modes.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (legal) application; contribution is incremental and narrow.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention under insufficient context

title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented LMs with a Two-stage Consistency Learning Compressor
authors: Chuankai Xu; Dongming Zhao; Bo Wang; Hanwen Xing
why_relevant: Proposes a post-retrieval compressor explicitly aimed at filtering noisy/extraneous retrieved content and improving robustness/faithfulness of RAG outputs, relevant to noisy retrieval mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a compression/distillation method rather than a dedicated robustness study; limited analysis of noise/conflict scenarios.

title: Evaluating the Retrieval Component in LLM-Based Question Answering Systems
authors: Ashkan Alinejad; Krtin Kumar; Ali Vahdat
why_relevant: Proposes an LLM-based framework for evaluating retriever quality in RAG that accounts for LLMs' ability to ignore irrelevant contexts, addressing limitations of conventional IR metrics. Relevant to evaluation of retrieval reliability under noisy/imperfect retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on evaluation methodology rather than directly on robustness, conflict, or adversarial issues.

title: Exploiting Web Search Tools of AI Agents for Data Exfiltration
authors: Dennis Rall; Bernhard Bauer; Mohit Mittal; Thomas Fraunholz
why_relevant: Empirically evaluates indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM agents using web-search/RAG tools for data exfiltration, relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent tool-calling security rather than RAG retrieval pipeline robustness specifically.

title: FACTUM: Mechanistic Detection of Citation Hallucination in Long-Form RAG
authors: Maxime Dassen; Rebecca Kotula; Kenton Murray; Andrew Yates; Dawn Lawrie; Efsun Kayi; James Mayfield; Kevin Duh
why_relevant: Proposes a mechanistic detector for citation hallucination in long-form RAG by decoupling attention (context) vs FFN (parametric) pathways, directly relevant to parametric-vs-retrieved conflict and reliability/calibration of RAG outputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on citation attribution hallucination detection via interpretability, not broader robustness; somewhat tangential to noise/attack/OOD topics.

title: FAITH: Factuality Alignment through Integrating Trustworthiness and Honestness
authors: Xiaoning Dong; Chengyan Wu; Yajie Wen; Yu Chen; Yun Xue; Jing Zhang; Wei Xu; Bolei Ma
why_relevant: FAITH is a post-training method for factuality alignment that integrates uncertainty estimation (consistency, semantic entropy) with a RAG module to rectify low-confidence responses, relevant to calibration/control and knowing when to trust internal vs external knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on factuality alignment via uncertainty-aware RL; RAG is auxiliary rather than the core robustness contribution.

title: FIT-RAG: Black-Box RAG with Factual Information and Token Reduction
authors: Yuren Mao; Xuemei Dong; Wenyi Xu; Yunjun Gao; Bin Wei; Ying Zhang
why_relevant: FIT-RAG introduces a self-knowledge recognizer to decide when augmentation is needed and a token reducer to filter unnecessary sub-documents, addressing when-to-retrieve and noisy/irrelevant context issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is primarily on efficiency and black-box augmentation, not explicitly on adversarial robustness or conflict.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (when to retrieve / filter)

title: Fast and Faithful: Real-Time Verification for Long-Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Xunzhuo Liu; Bowei He; Xue Liu; Haichen Zhang; Huamin Chen
why_relevant: Proposes a real-time faithfulness verifier for long-document RAG to detect unsupported/hallucinated responses, relevant to grounding verification and control mechanisms for unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on long-context verification engineering rather than directly on noise, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Faux Polyglot: A Study on Information Disparity in Multilingual Large Language Models
authors: Nikhil Sharma; Kenton Murray; Ziang Xiao
why_relevant: Studies inter-context knowledge conflicts in multilingual RAG, showing language-based biases in retrieval and generation when conflicting evidence appears across languages.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on linguistic/cultural bias rather than core robustness mechanisms; uses synthetic fictional data.

title: FlashRT: Towards Computationally and Memory Efficient Red-Teaming for Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
authors: Yanting Wang; Chenlong Yin; Ying Chen; Jinyuan Jia
why_relevant: Proposes an efficient optimization-based red-teaming framework for prompt injection and knowledge corruption attacks against long-context LLMs, directly applicable to RAG security evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency of attack optimization rather than RAG-specific defenses or evaluation; relevance is mainly as a red-teaming tool.

title: Flooding Spread of Manipulated Knowledge in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Communities
authors: Tianjie Ju; Yiting Wang; Xinbei Ma; Pengzhou Cheng; Haodong Zhao; Yulong Wang; Lifeng Liu; Jian Xie; Zhuosheng Zhang; Gongshen Liu
why_relevant: Demonstrates how manipulated knowledge can persist and spread via RAG when benign agents store and retrieve poisoned chat histories, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora in multi-agent settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is on multi-agent knowledge spread rather than RAG robustness; RAG persistence is a secondary contribution.

title: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
authors: Imene Kerboua; Sahar Omidi Shayegan; Megh Thakkar; Xing Han Lù; Léo Boisvert; Massimo Caccia; Jérémy Espinas; Alexandre Aussem; Véronique Eglin; Alexandre Lacoste
why_relevant: FocusAgent uses LLM-based retrieval to prune noisy web observations and defend against indirect prompt injection attacks (banners, pop-ups), tackling both noisy context and adversarial corruption in a retrieval-augmented agent setting.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on web agents rather than general RAG over document corpora; relevance is via analogy to context filtering and injection defense.

title: GOLD PANNING: Strategic Context Shuffling for Needle-in-Haystack Reasoning
authors: Adam Byerly; Daniel Khashabi
why_relevant: Addresses position bias in long-context/RAG retrieval via Bayesian reordering, relevant to distraction and inference-time control over noisy contexts.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on needle-in-haystack position bias rather than core RAG robustness issues like conflict or adversarial corruption.

title: GRAMMAR: Grounded and Modular Methodology for Assessment of Closed-Domain Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
authors: Xinzhe Li; Ming Liu; Shang Gao
why_relevant: Proposes a modular evaluation framework for closed-domain RAG that diagnoses whether failures stem from retrieval or LM, including robustness to query form variations. Relevant to evaluation methodology for unreliable RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on closed-domain evaluation and diagnostic protocol rather than directly studying noise, conflict, or adversarial attacks.

title: Give LLMs a Security Course: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Knowledge Injection
authors: Bo Lin; Shangwen Wang; Yihao Qin; Liqian Chen; Xiaoguang Mao
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against knowledge base poisoning in retrieval-augmented code generation, directly addressing adversarial corruption in RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation security rather than general RAG robustness.

title: Granite Guardian
authors: Inkit Padhi; Manish Nagireddy; Giandomenico Cornacchia; Subhajit Chaudhury; Tejaswini Pedapati; Pierre Dognin; Keerthiram Murugesan; Erik Miehling; Martín Santillán Cooper; Kieran Fraser; Giulio Zizzo; Muhammad Zaid Hameed; Mark Purcell; Michael Desmond; Qian Pan; Zahra Ashktorab; Inge Vejsbjerg; Elizabeth M. Daly; Michael Hind; Werner Geyer; Ambrish Rawat; Kush R. Varshney; Prasanna Sattigeri
why_relevant: Granite Guardian provides RAG-specific risk detection including context relevance, groundedness, and answer relevance, which directly relates to filtering unreliable evidence and detecting hallucinations in RAG pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a general-purpose safety guardrail model; RAG robustness is one of several capabilities rather than the central focus.
suggested_section: Calibration and control / guardrails for RAG

title: GraphSteal: Structural Knowledge Stealing from Graph RAG via Traversal Reconstruction
authors: Jinze Gu; Qinghua Mao; Xi Lin; Jun Wu
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box extraction attack against Graph RAG that reconstructs the underlying knowledge graph, exposing a privacy attack surface relevant to adversarial threats on RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy/structural extraction rather than poisoning, injection, or robustness of generation; narrower fit to the survey's adversarial-corruption theme.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG

title: HAVE: Head-Adaptive Gating and ValuE Calibration for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models
authors: Xin Tong; Zhi Lin; Jingya Wang; Bo Jin
why_relevant: HAVE is a decoding-time method targeting hallucinations in RAG/long-context settings by calibrating attention-based evidence and using uncertainty-scaled fusion, relevant to context-faithful decoding and calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on decoding mechanics rather than retrieval robustness per se; tangential to noise/attack aspects.

title: Harnessing RLHF for Robust Unanswerability Recognition and Trustworthy Response Generation in LLMs
authors: Shuyuan Lin; Lei Duan; Philip Hughes; Yuxuan Sheng
why_relevant: Proposes RLHF-based training for LLMs to detect unanswerable questions and abstain, addressing knowledge boundary awareness and hallucination reduction in conversational IR.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on unanswerability/abstention rather than full RAG pipeline robustness; quality of arXiv-only paper uncertain.

title: Improving Factuality with Explicit Working Memory
authors: Mingda Chen; Yang Li; Karthik Padthe; Rulin Shao; Alicia Sun; Luke Zettlemoyer; Gargi Ghosh; Wen-tau Yih
why_relevant: EWE proposes adaptive retrieval with fact-checking feedback and memory updates to mitigate hallucination in long-form RAG, relevant to when-to-retrieve/re-retrieve and factuality control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on factuality enhancement rather than explicitly studying noise, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Improving Reliability and Explainability of Medical Question Answering through Atomic Fact Checking in Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
authors: Juraj Vladika; Annika Domres; Mai Nguyen; Rebecca Moser; Jana Nano; Felix Busch; Lisa C. Adams; Keno K. Bressem; Denise Bernhardt; Stephanie E. Combs; Kai J. Borm; Florian Matthes; Jan C. Peeken
why_relevant: Proposes atomic fact-checking post-hoc to detect and correct hallucinations in medical RAG, addressing reliability and explainability of retrieved-grounded answers.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical) application; not a general robustness study.

title: KnowGuard: Knowledge-Driven Abstention for Multi-Round Clinical Reasoning
authors: Xilin Dang; Kexin Chen; Xiaorui Su; Ayush Noori; Iñaki Arango; Lucas Vittor; Xinyi Long; Yuyang Du; Marinka Zitnik; Pheng Ann Heng
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge-graph-grounded abstention method for multi-round clinical QA, addressing when LLMs should refrain from answering under insufficient evidence—directly relevant to abstention and calibration control under uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (clinical) and focused on KG exploration rather than general RAG robustness; abstention is the main contribution.

title: L-RAG: Balancing Context and Retrieval with Entropy-Based Lazy Loading
authors: Sergii Voloshyn
why_relevant: Proposes entropy-based gating to decide when to retrieve, directly addressing adaptive retrieval and uncertainty-driven control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency rather than robustness; small-scale evaluation on SQuAD 2.0 with Phi-2.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: LIT-RAGBench: Benchmarking Generator Capabilities of Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Koki Itai; Shunichi Hasegawa; Yuta Yamamoto; Gouki Minegishi; Masaki Otsuki
why_relevant: Introduces a generator benchmark covering abstention when evidence is missing, alongside integration, reasoning, logic, and table understanding—relevant for evaluation of RAG robustness and abstention behavior.
why_not_or_caveat: Small Japanese-origin dataset (114 questions); focuses on generator capabilities broadly rather than centrally on noise/conflict/adversarial robustness.

title: LLM Embedding-based Attribution (LEA): Quantifying Source Contributions to Generative Model's Response for Vulnerability Analysis
authors: Reza Fayyazi; Michael Zuzak; Shanchieh Jay Yang
why_relevant: Proposes an attribution metric (LEA) that quantifies whether LLM outputs rely on retrieved context vs internal parametric knowledge, and evaluates behavior under valid, generic, and incorrect retrieval—directly relevant to knowledge conflict and auditing RAG reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to CVE/vulnerability analysis; method is more about attribution/auditing than improving robustness itself.

title: LLM Robustness Against Misinformation in Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Alexander Bondarenko; Adrian Viehweger
why_relevant: Evaluates LLM robustness in RAG against prompt-injection of misinformation in the biomedical domain, using ASR and accuracy drop metrics across multiple models.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and limited methodological novelty; focuses only on augmented generation, not retrieval.

title: LLMs Should Express Uncertainty Explicitly
authors: Junyu Guo; Shangding Gu; Ming Jin; Costas Spanos; Javad Lavaei
why_relevant: Trains LLMs to explicitly express uncertainty (verbalized confidence or <uncertain> marker) that can trigger adaptive retrieval and abstention, directly relevant to calibration/control for when to retrieve.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on uncertainty expression broadly; RAG triggering is one application, not the central study.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control (when to retrieve / abstain)

title: LeakSealer: A Semisupervised Defense for LLMs Against Prompt Injection and Leakage Attacks
authors: Francesco Panebianco; Stefano Bonfanti; Francesco Trovò; Michele Carminati
why_relevant: Proposes a defense framework against prompt injection and PII leakage attacks targeting RAG systems, relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader on LLM jailbreak/PII leakage detection rather than RAG-specific evidence robustness; RAG is only one of the scenarios.

title: Learned Hallucination Detection in Black-Box LLMs using Token-level Entropy Production Rate
authors: Charles Moslonka; Hicham Randrianarivo; Arthur Garnier; Emmanuel Malherbe
why_relevant: Proposes a token-level entropy-based hallucination detector for black-box LLMs, applicable to RAG outputs for uncertainty quantification and abstention.
why_not_or_caveat: Not RAG-specific; focuses on generic hallucination detection with one RAG case study.

title: Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents
authors: Mehmet Iscan
why_relevant: Proposes a risk-sensitive contextual bandit controller that decides whether to inject retrieved memory, abstain, ask for feedback, or skip retrieval, with explicit false-positive penalties. Directly addresses when-to-retrieve/trust and abstention in an agentic RAG-like memory setting.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain is narrow (coding-agent issue memory) and evaluation is small-scale, deterministic proxy rather than full RAG benchmarks.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: when to retrieve and abstain

title: MALM: A Multi-Information Adapter for Large Language Models to Mitigate Hallucination
authors: Ao Jia; Haiming Wu; Guohui Yao; Dawei Song; Songkun Ji; Yazhou Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes an adapter to mitigate input-, context-, and fact-conflicting hallucinations, including in RAG settings with noisy retrieved documents.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader hallucination mitigation via graph adapter; RAG robustness is secondary.

title: MMKB-RAG: A Multi-Modal Knowledge-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework
authors: Zihan Ling; Zhiyao Guo; Yixuan Huang; Yi An; Shuai Xiao; Jinsong Lan; Xiaoyong Zhu; Bo Zheng
why_relevant: Proposes a multi-modal RAG framework that decides when to retrieve, filters irrelevant documents, and reranks for consistency, addressing noisy retrieval and retrieval control in MLLMs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multi-modal VQA; robustness contributions are incremental filtering/self-RAG-style tagging rather than novel calibration analysis.
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve and filter

title: MTRAG: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Yannis Katsis; Sara Rosenthal; Kshitij Fadnis; Chulaka Gunasekara; Young-Suk Lee; Lucian Popa; Vraj Shah; Huaiyu Zhu; Danish Contractor; Marina Danilevsky
why_relevant: MTRAG is a multi-turn RAG benchmark that explicitly tests unanswerable questions and non-standalone questions, evaluating how RAG systems handle these challenging cases relevant to abstention and uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a general multi-turn RAG benchmark; robustness aspects (unanswerability) are one of several dimensions rather than the central focus.

title: MedRAGChecker: Claim-Level Verification for Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yuelyu Ji; Min Gu Kwak; Hang Zhang; Xizhi Wu; Chenyu Li; Yanshan Wang
why_relevant: Proposes claim-level verification framework for biomedical RAG that diagnoses faithfulness, under-evidence, contradiction, and safety-critical errors, helping disentangle retrieval vs generation failures.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical); primarily a verification/evaluation tool rather than a robustness method.
suggested_section: Evaluation and Metrics for RAG Faithfulness

title: MedTrust-RAG: Evidence Verification and Trust Alignment for Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yingpeng Ning; Yuanyuan Sun; Ling Luo; Yanhua Wang; Yuchen Pan; Hongfei Lin
why_relevant: Proposes iterative retrieval-verification with citation-grounded reasoning and structured refusal (Negative Knowledge Assertions) to mitigate post-retrieval noise and hallucinations in biomedical RAG, addressing noisy evidence and abstention.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and primarily an applied method; not a general robustness study.

title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
authors: Balachandra Devarangadi Sunil; Isheeta Sinha; Piyush Maheshwari; Shantanu Todmal; Shreyan Mallik; Shuchi Mishra
why_relevant: Studies memory poisoning attacks (MINJA) on memory/RAG-augmented LLM agents and proposes trust-scoring and memory sanitization defenses with calibration analysis, relevant to adversarial corruption and defense calibration in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on agent memory rather than standard retrieval corpora; narrow EHR domain case study.

title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
authors: Liyan Tang; Philippe Laban; Greg Durrett
why_relevant: Provides an efficient fact-checker and unified benchmark (LLM-AggreFact) for verifying LLM outputs against grounding documents, directly useful for evaluating RAG faithfulness and detecting unsupported claims.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on fact-checking/grounding verification rather than retrieval robustness, conflict, or attacks directly.

title: Mitigating Hallucination in Financial Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Fine-Grained Knowledge Verification
authors: Taoye Yin; Haoyuan Hu; Yaxin Fan; Xinhao Chen; Xinya Wu; Kai Deng; Kezun Zhang; Feng Wang
why_relevant: Addresses hallucinations in RAG where generated answers conflict with retrieved evidence, using fine-grained faithfulness rewards via RL to improve context compliance.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (financial) and a fairly narrow methodological contribution; not a central robustness paper.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Resolution of Recommendation Conflicts in Multimorbidity Clinical Guidelines
authors: Shiyao Xie; Jian Du
why_relevant: Addresses inter-document knowledge conflicts in retrieved clinical guidelines, proposing a neuro-symbolic SAT-based pipeline to detect retrieved-vs-retrieved conflicts before RAG, and provides a benchmark for guideline conflict detection.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (clinical guidelines) and focuses on knowledge base curation rather than RAG inference robustness directly.

title: On the Consistency of Multilingual Context Utilization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jirui Qi; Raquel Fernández; Arianna Bisazza
why_relevant: Studies how LLMs in multilingual RAG handle distracting passages across languages and consistency of context utilization, relevant to distraction and robustness evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is multilingual consistency rather than core robustness; distraction analysis is a secondary aspect.

title: On the Robustness of LLM-Based Dense Retrievers: A Systematic Analysis of Generalizability and Stability
authors: Yongkang Li; Panagiotis Eustratiadis; Yixing Fan; Evangelos Kanoulas
why_relevant: Systematic robustness study of LLM-based dense retrievers covering query perturbations and corpus poisoning attacks, relevant to retrieval-side noise and adversarial corruption components of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on the retriever in isolation rather than end-to-end RAG generation robustness.

title: Ontology-Guided Neuro-Symbolic Inference: Grounding Language Models with Mathematical Domain Knowledge
authors: Marcelo Labre
why_relevant: The paper empirically shows that retrieval quality determines whether RAG helps or hurts: high-relevance ontology context improves accuracy while irrelevant retrieved definitions actively degrade performance, directly illustrating distraction and noisy retrieval effects.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (mathematics with OpenMath ontology) rather than a general robustness study; contribution to robustness is incidental.

title: PAIRS: Parametric-Verified Adaptive Information Retrieval and Selection for Efficient RAG
authors: Wang Chen; Guanqiang Qi; Weikang Li; Yang Li; Deguo Xia; Jizhou Huang
why_relevant: PAIRS adaptively decides when to retrieve by comparing parametric vs pseudo-context answers, and filters retrieved documents to mitigate irrelevant retrievals—directly relevant to adaptive retrieval control and noisy retrieval filtering.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on efficiency/accuracy rather than explicit robustness, calibration, or adversarial settings.
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve

title: Panini: Continual Learning in Token Space via Structured Memory
authors: Shreyas Rajesh; Pavan Holur; Mehmet Yigit Turali; Chenda Duan; Vwani Roychowdhury
why_relevant: Panini explicitly targets reliability issues in RAG: it reduces unsupported/hallucinated generation from irrelevant chunk context and evaluates abstention on unanswerable queries via curated splits.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a structured-memory/efficiency method; robustness/abstention is a secondary contribution rather than the central focus.
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention / Structured memory alternatives to chunk RAG

title: Parametric Knowledge and Retrieval Behavior in RAG Fine-Tuning for Electronic Design Automation
authors: Julian Oestreich; Maximilian Bley; Frank Binder; Lydia Müller; Maksym Sydorenko; André Alcalde
why_relevant: Studies RAG fine-tuning robustness under varying retrieval conditions (relevant, irrelevant, noisy, missing) and proposes a triple-based evaluation metric (PKP) that disentangles parametric vs retrieved knowledge, relevant to evaluation and knowledge conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (EDA) and focuses on a custom metric rather than general robustness methods.
suggested_section: Evaluation and metrics for RAG under noisy retrieval

title: Permissive Information-Flow Analysis for Large Language Models
authors: Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui; Radhika Gaonkar; Boris Köpf; David Krueger; Andrew Paverd; Ahmed Salem; Shruti Tople; Lukas Wutschitz; Menglin Xia; Santiago Zanella-Béguelin
why_relevant: Proposes an information-flow label propagation defense for RAG/LLM-agent settings where retrieved documents may be poisoned or untrusted, addressing integrity/confidentiality robustness in retrieval pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on system-level taint tracking rather than core RAG robustness methods; tangential to noise/conflict/calibration themes.

title: PlanGuard: Defending Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection via Planning-based Consistency Verification
authors: Guangyu Gong; Zizhuang Deng
why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection in LLM agents using retrieved content, relevant to adversarial corruption of external/retrieved context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on agent tool-use rather than RAG QA; IPI defense via plan consistency is tangential to retrieval pipeline robustness.
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Prompt Injection Defenses

title: PluriHopRAG: Exhaustive, Recall-Sensitive QA Through Corpus-Specific Document Structure Learning
authors: Mykolas Sveistrys; Richard Kunert
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark and method explicitly targeting distractor-heavy, recall-sensitive retrieval over repetitive corpora, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval challenges in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on exhaustive aggregation QA rather than core robustness topics like conflict, attacks, or calibration.

title: Poison-RAG: Adversarial Data Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Recommender Systems
authors: Fatemeh Nazary; Yashar Deldjoo; Tommaso di Noia
why_relevant: Proposes a data poisoning attack on RAG-based recommender systems by manipulating item metadata, relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval corpora.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to recommender systems rather than general QA RAG; narrower scope.

title: Prompt Control-Flow Integrity: A Priority-Aware Runtime Defense Against Prompt Injection in LLM Systems
authors: Md Takrim Ul Alam; Akif Islam; Mohd Ruhul Ameen; Abu Saleh Musa Miah; Jungpil Shin
why_relevant: Proposes a runtime middleware defense against prompt injection attacks, including indirect injection via RAG retrieved documents, enforcing priority among system/developer/user/retrieved segments.
why_not_or_caveat: Evaluated on a small custom synthetic benchmark; defense is generic to LLM APIs rather than RAG-specific, and claims (100% interception, 0% FPR) are limited in scope.
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against indirect prompt injection

title: Proof-Carrying Numbers (PCN): A Protocol for Trustworthy Numeric Answers from LLMs via Claim Verification
